> **Amended 2026-10-21:** the approved build uses a FastAPI + MySQL backend and

## 1. Project Goal

Build a task planner mobile application that helps the user organize tasks and decide what to work on next.

The app should be simple, reliable, easy to use, and usable without an internet connection.

- Mobile application built with Flutter and Dart.

## 3. First Release (MVP)

display.text:
# Project Brief ÔÇö Task Planner

> **Amended 2026-10-21:** the approved build uses a FastAPI + MySQL backend and
> is online-only; the offline-first constraints below are superseded. See
> `docs/decisions/2026-10-21-fastapi-mysql-backend.md`. Task editing remains a
> required MVP feature.

## 1. Project Goal

Build a task planner mobile application that helps the user organize tasks and decide what to work on next.

The app should be simple, reliable, easy to use, and usable without an internet connection.

## 2. Target Platform

- Mobile application built with Flutter and Dart.
- Android is the initial target.
- Keep the architecture open to supporting iOS later.

## 3. First Release (MVP)

The first release should focus on essential task management:

- Create a task.
- Edit a task.
- Delete a task.
- Mark a task as completed.
- Reopen a completed task.
- Assign a priority.
- Optionally set a due date.
- View today's tasks.
- View upcoming and overdue tasks.
- Save tasks locally so they remain available after closing and reopening the app.
- Log in with an account (login page).
- Create an account (sign-up page).

## 4. Initial User Experience

The user should be able to open the app and quickly understand:

- What needs to be done today.
- Which tasks are overdue.
- Which tasks are most important.
- What has already been completed.

Avoid unnecessary screens and complicated workflows.

The app opens on a login page; new users reach the sign-up page from there.

## 5. Business Rules

- A task must have a title.
- A task is not required to have a due date.
- New tasks are incomplete by default.
- Completing a task records when it was completed.
- Reopening a task clears its completion timestamp.
- An incomplete task is overdue when its due date has passed.
- Completed tasks are not considered overdue.
- Task data must persist locally.
- Using the app requires an account; accounts are stored locally on the device.
- Login uses a unique email and a password (stored as a salted hash, never plain text).
- A self-registered account stays pending and cannot log in until the relevant project owner confirms it.
- Approval records the confirming project owner's id (`approved_by`).
- Roles are admin, project owner, and user, and they are cumulative: an admin can do everything a project owner and a user can do, and a project owner everything a user can do.
- Only an admin creates projects, assigns project owners, and manages roles.
- A project owner confirms new members of their own project and manages its tasks and assignments.

## 6. Constraints

- Offline-first: core functionality must work without internet access.
- Multiple user accounts stored locally on a single device; no backend server is required for the initial version.
- Keep the implementation simple and maintainable.
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies and architectural complexity.
- Do not introduce AI features until the core task planner works reliably.

## 7. Decisions Not Yet Finalized

The following require discussion before implementation:

- Whether tasks should also support categories alongside projects.
- Whether reminders and notifications belong in the first release.
- Whether the app needs manual backup and restore.
- Whether the main planner should show a daily view, weekly view, or both.
- Which priority levels and task statuses are needed.
- The final architecture, database, and state-management choices.
- How the very first admin account is created on a fresh install.
- Password recovery or reset without a backend (for example, admin resets passwords).
- Which events trigger email notifications (proposed: new sign-up, approval or rejection, task assignment).

Do not silently decide these questions if they materially affect the design.

## 8. Development Rules

- Inspect the existing repository before proposing changes.
- Reuse existing code and project conventions where appropriate.
- Propose architectural changes and wait for explicit approval.
- Do not implement unapproved features or install dependencies without approval.
- Keep changes small and test them independently.
- Report what was changed, what was tested, and any remaining issues.

## 9. Initial Development Objective

Start with discovery, not implementation.

Review this brief alongside the repository and proposed architecture. Identify missing requirements, important questions, risks, and the smallest useful next step.

Do not modify files or write application code during discovery. Present recommendations and wait for approval.

## Task Assignment

Each task has at most one assignee.

The assignee can be either:

- **A person** ÔÇö identified by name, with a position such as Developer, Project Manager, or Business Analyst. Exactly one person is responsible.
- **A project** ÔÇö the task is assigned to the project as a whole, meaning several people are affected; no single person is named.

Task rules:

- A task belongs to a project.
- A task can be assigned to that project as a whole (no individual assignee) or to one person from the project ÔÇö never both at the same time.
- A person assignee must belong to the task's project.
- The assignee's position should be available when viewing the task.
- The assignee should be optional unless the user decides otherwise.
- The app should support assigning tasks to different people, not only the current user.

## Assignee Management

The application should provide a way to manage assignee information so the same person does not need to be entered from scratch for every task.

The exact management interface and data model must be proposed before implementation.

Each assignee belongs to a project via a `project_id` foreign key.

## Accounts and Roles

- The app opens on a login page; a sign-up page creates a new account.
- An admin creates each project and assigns its project owner.
- New users are created by an admin, by a project owner, or by self-registration.
- Approval records which project owner confirmed the account.

# Task Planner

phpMyAdmin instance for local development.

The app is online-only: it talks to the API and stores no task data locally.
The API owns authentication, roles, membership approval, and task rules.

On a fresh clone, after installing the prerequisites below:

```powershell

<http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs>, and phpMyAdmin at <http://127.0.0.1:8080>.
The sections below explain each step and the Android/device variants.

## 1. Prerequisites

- Git.
- Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS) or Docker Engine with Compose v2.
- Flutter 3.47+ and Dart 3.13+.
- Android Studio, Android SDK, and an emulator for Android development.
- Optional: VS Code. Open the repository folder and accept the recommended
  Flutter, Dart, Python, and Docker extensions.
- Python 3.11+ only if you run the backend directly on the host instead of
  in Docker.

Flutter stays on the host rather than in a Dev Container so emulator, USB
device, and desktop debugging work normally. Only the API, MySQL, and
phpMyAdmin run in Docker.

Verify the tools from a new terminal:

```powershell
docker --version
docker compose version
flutter doctor
```

For Android, accept the SDK licenses and check for an emulator:

```powershell
flutter doctor --android-licenses
flutter emulators
adb devices
```

If `docker` is not found on Windows, make sure Docker Desktop is running and
open a new terminal. A per-user install may need Docker Desktop's
`resources\bin` directory on `PATH`.

## 2. Clone the repository

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/chocksma3iil/Task_planner_mobile_app.git
cd Task_planner_mobile_app
```

Use your fork instead of the upstream URL if you have one.

## 3. Configure environment variables

The Docker stack reads the root `.env`. It is Git-ignored. Skip this copy if
`.env` already exists.

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` and replace the placeholder passwords and `SECRET_KEY`. Use
URL-safe characters in `MYSQL_PASSWORD` because it becomes part of the
database URL. The defaults for ports are:

- API: `8000`
- phpMyAdmin: `8080`
- MySQL: `3306` inside the Docker network only

The API and phpMyAdmin bind to `127.0.0.1` by default. MySQL has no host port,
so the stack does not conflict with a MySQL installation on your machine and
does not expose the database to the LAN.

`backend/.env` is only for running FastAPI directly on the host. It is not
needed for the Compose flow. Never commit either `.env` file or use development
credentials for shared or production systems.

## 4. Start Docker services

From the repository root:

```powershell
docker compose up --build -d
docker compose ps
```

Wait until `mysql` and `api` are healthy. First start pulls images and
initializes the database, so it can take a few minutes.

Useful commands:

```powershell
docker compose logs -f api
docker compose logs -f mysql
docker compose down
```

`docker compose down` keeps the named database volume. Do **not** use
`docker compose down -v` unless you intend to delete all local Docker database
data.

## 5. Initialize the database

The API container runs this before Uvicorn starts:

```text
alembic upgrade head
```

On a fresh volume this applies `backend/alembic/versions/0001_initial.py` and
creates `projects`, `assignees`, `tasks`, and `alembic_version`. The MySQL init
script also creates `task_planner_test` and grants the app user access, so the
pytest suite works without manual database setup.

Verify the tables:

```powershell
docker compose exec mysql mysql -utask_planner -p task_planner -e "SHOW TABLES;"
```

The final `task_planner` argument selects the database; without it, MySQL
returns `ERROR 1046 (3D000): No database selected`. Use the `MYSQL_PASSWORD`
value from `.env` when prompted. You can also inspect
`alembic_version` there. The Compose database is separate from any MySQL
installation already running on the host; it does not overwrite or reset it.

If you have an older database created by `create_all` rather than Alembic, do
not run migrations blindly. Back it up first; after verifying the schema
matches, `alembic stamp 0001_initial` can mark it as current. Never do this
against a shared database without authorization.

## 6. Run the Flutter application

From the repository root, in a second terminal:

```powershell
cd task_planner
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

The app uses `http://localhost:8000/api/v1` by default, which works for Windows
desktop, web, and the iOS simulator. For other targets, pass the full base URL,
including `/api/v1`.

| Target | Command |
|---|---|
| Windows desktop | `flutter run -d windows` |
| Android emulator | `flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8000/api/v1` |
| Android physical device over USB | `adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000` then `flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/v1` |
| Physical device over LAN | Set `API_BIND=0.0.0.0` in `.env`, run `docker compose up -d api`, then use `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://YOUR_LAN_IP:8000/api/v1` |

and allow port `8000` through the host firewall if needed. The development API
uses HTTP; release builds should use HTTPS. Android debug builds allow local
HTTP. iOS blocks cleartext HTTP by default, so iOS device development needs
HTTPS or a reviewed ATS exception.

The first account registered on a fresh database becomes the admin. Later
sign-ups join a project as pending members until the project owner or an admin
confirms them. Passwords must be at least 8 characters.

## 7. Access phpMyAdmin

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080>. The login page is already configured for the
local `mysql` container. These are the MySQL credentials, not the app account
you create in Flutter.

- Username: `task_planner`
- Password: `MYSQL_PASSWORD` from the root `.env`

phpMyAdmin is bound to loopback only. Do not expose it publicly.

## 8. Run tests and checks

Backend tests run inside the API container against `task_planner_test`:

```powershell
docker compose exec api python -m pytest tests -q
```

Flutter checks do not need the backend:

```powershell
cd task_planner
flutter analyze
flutter test
```

The Flutter widget tests use an in-memory fake API client. The backend test
suite truncates its test tables between tests, so `TEST_DATABASE_URL` must
always point at a disposable local database.

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| `docker: command not found` | Start Docker Desktop and open a new terminal; verify `PATH`. |
| `docker-credential-desktop` not found | Open a new terminal after installing Docker Desktop, or add its `resources\bin` directory to `PATH`. |
| Port `8000` or `8080` already in use | Stop the local service or change `API_PORT` / `PHPMYADMIN_PORT` in `.env`, then restart Compose. |
| API container is unhealthy | Run `docker compose logs api`; confirm `mysql` is healthy and the API uses hostname `mysql`, not `localhost`. |
| phpMyAdmin cannot log in | Use user `task_planner` and the password from `.env`; leave the default server. Check `docker compose logs mysql`. |
| `ERROR 1046 (3D000): No database selected` | Add the database name to the MySQL command: `docker compose exec mysql mysql -utask_planner -p task_planner -e "SHOW TABLES;"`. |
| `Access denied` after changing MySQL passwords | MySQL applies `MYSQL_*` values only when the volume is first initialized. Use the original credentials or change the database user explicitly; do not delete the volume without a backup. |
| Alembic says a table already exists | The database was not created by Alembic. Use a fresh volume, or back up and stamp only after verifying the schema. |
| Android app cannot reach the API | Use `10.0.2.2` for the emulator, or `adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000` for USB. Debug builds allow local HTTP; release builds do not. |
| `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is missing | Use the Compose test command above, or create `backend/.env` for a host-run backend. |

## 10. Shared development database (optional)

This repository does not create or expose a shared database. If your team
provides one, the maintainer supplies the host, port, database name, username,
password, and phpMyAdmin URL separately. Do not put those credentials in the
root `.env` used by the local Compose stack and never commit them.

For a shared database, run only the API and the Flutter app locally:

```powershell
$env:DATABASE_URL = "mysql+pymysql://USER:PASSWORD@SHARED_HOST:3306/task_planner?charset=utf8mb4"
$env:CREATE_SCHEMA_ON_STARTUP = "false"

cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

- If you run the test suite, set `TEST_DATABASE_URL` to a separate disposable
  local database. The test suite truncates tables; never point it at shared
  data.
- Do not run `alembic upgrade head` or any write operation against shared data
  without explicit authorization.
- If a shared phpMyAdmin instance is provided, use its URL. The local
  phpMyAdmin service is configured for the local `mysql` container only.

## Further reading

- `backend/README.md` ÔÇö API setup, configuration, endpoints, and migrations.
- `task_planner/README.md` ÔÇö Flutter setup, architecture, and file layout.
- `docs/decisions/2026-10-22-local-development-onboarding.md` ÔÇö decision record
  for this setup.
- `docs/decisions/2026-10-21-fastapi-mysql-backend.md` ÔÇö backend architecture.

1: # Task Planner
2: 
3: Mobile task planner built with Flutter, backed by a FastAPI + MySQL server.
4: Three roles (admin, project owner, user), projects, members, and tasks that can
5: be created, edited, completed, reopened, and deleted.
6: The app is online-only: it talks to the API and stores no tasks locally.
7: 
8: For the complete local stack (Docker, MySQL, phpMyAdmin, API, and app), start
9: with the root [`../README.md`](../README.md).
10: 
11: ## Prerequisites
12: 
13: - [Flutter SDK](https://docs.flutter.dev/get-started/install) 3.47+ (Dart 3.13+)
14: - Android Studio, Android SDK, and an emulator for Android development
15: - A platform to run on: Android emulator, iOS simulator, Windows, or web
16: - The backend running (Compose is recommended; see `../README.md`)
17: 
18: Verify your setup:
19: 
20: ```bash
21: flutter doctor
22: ```
23: 
24: ## Start the backend first
25: 
26: From the repository root, the recommended path is:
27: 
28: ```powershell
29: docker compose up --build -d
30: ```
31: 
32: The API listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`; feature routes live under `/api/v1`
33: and `GET /health` stays unversioned.
34: 
35: For a host-run backend instead:
36: 
37: ```powershell
38: cd ../backend
39: .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
40: uvicorn app.main:app --reload
41: ```
42: 
43: ## Run the app
44: 
45: From the `task_planner/` directory:
46: 
47: ```bash
48: flutter pub get
49: flutter run
50: ```
51: 
52: The app calls `http://localhost:8000/api/v1` unless you override the full base
53: URL (the version prefix is part of it):
54: 
55: ```bash
56: # Android emulator reaches the host machine at 10.0.2.2
57: flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8000/api/v1
58: 
59: # Physical Android device over USB (requires the API on host port 8000)
60: adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000
61: flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/v1
62: 
63: # Physical device over LAN: bind the API to the LAN and use your machine's IP
64: flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8000/api/v1
65: ```
66: 
67: For LAN access, set `API_BIND=0.0.0.0` in the root `.env`, then run
68: `docker compose up -d api` from the repository root so the port mapping is
69: recreated. Use this only on a trusted network. Android debug builds permit local
70: HTTP; release builds should use HTTPS. iOS blocks cleartext HTTP by default
71: and needs HTTPS or a reviewed ATS exception for device development.
72: 
73: On Windows you can run the desktop build directly:
74: 
75: ```bash
76: flutter run -d windows
77: ```
78: 
79: The first account you register becomes the admin (the server promotes the
80: first account on a fresh database). Everyone after that joins a project as a
81: pending member until the project owner or an admin confirms them. Passwords
82: must be at least 8 characters; emails are case-insensitive.
83: 
84: ## Test and analyze
85: 
86: ```bash
87: flutter analyze
88: flutter test
89: ```
90: 
91: Widget tests run against an in-memory fake of the API (`FakeApiClient`), so
92: they need no backend or database. The backend suite is documented in
93: `../backend/README.md`.
94: 
95: ## Architecture
96: 
97: **Layer-first modular monolith** ÔÇö one Flutter app plus one FastAPI service:
98: 
99: | Layer | Where | Rule |
100: |---|---|---|
101: | Presentation | `screens/`, `widgets/` | Screens, tabs, dialogs, and shared widgets. No HTTP and no business rules. |
102: | Application / state | `providers/`, `services/` | Riverpod providers wire services to the UI; services call the API and return typed models. |
103: | Domain | `models/`, `core/rules.dart` | JSON models and pure UX rules (overdue/due-today, role tabs). |
104: | Data | `services/api_client.dart`, `services/data_sync.dart` | The only place the app performs HTTP (bearer token, JSON, error mapping). |
105: | Cross-cutting | `core/`, `widgets/shared/` | Theme, formatters, positions, and reusable UI helpers. |
106: | DI | `main.dart`, `providers/api_providers.dart` | `main` builds `HttpApiClient` from `API_BASE_URL` and overrides `apiClientProvider`. |
107: | Navigation | `app/app.dart`, `app/router.dart` | `MaterialApp.router`; redirects: logged out ÔåÆ `/login`, logged in ÔåÆ `/home`. |
108: | Server | `../backend/` | FastAPI + MySQL. The server enforces access control, membership approval, and assignment rules. |
109: 
110: Dependency flow is one-directional: `screens/widgets ÔåÆ providers ÔåÆ services ÔåÆ
111: ApiClient ÔåÆ HTTP ÔåÆ backend`. The UI never calls the API directly. Business
112: rules are enforced server-side; `core/rules.dart` only shapes the UI, and
113: `backend/app/core/rules.py` mirrors the checks for the server.
114: 
115: Refresh strategy: mutations ping `DataSync`, and data streams (`watchFromApi`)
116: re-fetch in place without a loading flicker.
117: 
118: Stack: Flutter + Dart, flutter_riverpod (state/DI), go_router (navigation),
119: http (API calls), shared_preferences (theme preference only).
120: 
121: ## Project layout ÔÇö file by file
122: 
123: ```
124: lib/
125:   main.dart                    # Entry point: builds HttpApiClient from
126:                                # API_BASE_URL (default .../api/v1), overrides
127:                                # apiClientProvider, starts ProviderScope.
128:   app/
129:     app.dart                   # MaterialApp.router, light/dark theme selection.
130:     router.dart                # GoRouter routes + session redirects.
131:   core/
132:     formatters.dart            # initialsOf, formatDate.
133:     positions.dart             # Predefined job titles.
134:     rules.dart                 # Pure UX rules: canLogIn, isAdmin,
135:                                # visibleTabs, isOverdue/isDueToday/isUpcoming.
136:     theme.dart                 # buildTheme(Brightness) Material theme factory.
137:   models/
138:     account.dart               # Account (JSON key compatible with the old
139:                                # Assignee model; table remains `assignees`).
140:     project.dart               # Project.
141:     task.dart                  # Task.
142:     models.dart                # Barrel export.
143:   providers/
144:     api_providers.dart         # apiClientProvider (overridden in main).
145:     data_providers.dart        # Service providers + stream providers
146:                                # (projectsProvider, projectTasksProvider,
147:                                # myTasksProvider, visibleMembersProvider).
148:     session_providers.dart     # sessionUserIdProvider, currentUserProvider,
149:                                # logIn/logOut.
150:     theme_mode_provider.dart   # Persists light/dark/system in
151:                                # shared_preferences (device-level choice).
152:   services/
153:     api_client.dart            # ApiClient + HttpApiClient (bearer token, JSON,
154:                                # StateError/ArgumentError mapping, timeout).
155:     auth_service.dart          # Sign-up, login, token handling.
156:     data_sync.dart             # Global "data changed" signal + watchFromApi.
157:     member_service.dart        # Visible members, create, confirm, role change.
158:     project_service.dart       # Create/list projects, assign owner.
159:     task_service.dart          # Create/edit/complete/reopen/delete tasks.
160:   screens/
161:     login_screen.dart          # Email/password form ÔåÆ logIn().
162:     signup_screen.dart         # Self-registration (creates pending account).
163:     home_screen.dart           # Scaffold hosting the role-filtered tabs.
164:     projects_tab.dart          # Admin-only: create/manage projects + owners.
165:     members_tab.dart           # Members list scoped to the logged-in role.
166:     tasks_tab.dart             # Project-scoped task list (admin picks project).
167:     my_tasks_tab.dart          # Tasks assigned to the logged-in person.
168:   widgets/
169:     members/
170:       add_member_dialog.dart   # Collects the new active member.
171:       member_card.dart         # Roster row with status/role/confirm action.
172:     projects/
173:       create_project_dialog.dart
174:       project_card.dart        # Project summary + admin owner menu.
175:     settings/
176:       theme_picker.dart        # System / Light / Dark dialog.
177:     shared/
178:       app_snackbar.dart        # showAppSnackBar + userMessage helper.
179:       empty_state.dart         # Empty/no-match state (optionally scrollable).
180:       error_state.dart         # Error message with retry.
181:       position_field.dart      # Dropdown + custom job-title input.
182:       search_field.dart        # DebouncedSearchField.
183:       section_header.dart      # SectionHeader.
184:     tasks/
185:       priority_chip.dart
186:       swipe_background.dart
187:       task_filters.dart        # All/Today/Upcoming/Overdue chips.
188:       task_form_dialog.dart    # Create/edit dialog (returns TaskDraft).
189:       task_list.dart           # Reusable task list: search, stats, grouping,
190:                                # swipe/undo, tap-to-edit, pull-to-refresh.
191:       task_stats.dart
192:       task_tile.dart
193: test/
194:   rules_test.dart              # Unit tests for core/rules.dart.
195:   api_client_test.dart         # Error/token mapping of HttpApiClient.
196:   home_screen_test.dart        # Widget tests for the home screen and edit
197:                                # flow, driven by FakeApiClient.
198: ```
199: 
200: Other files and where they come from:
201: 
202: | Path | Origin |
203: |---|---|
204: | `pubspec.yaml` | Hand-written; declares dependencies. |
205: | `pubspec.lock`, `.dart_tool/`, `.flutter-plugins-dependencies` | Created by `flutter pub get`. |
206: | `analysis_options.yaml` | `flutter create` (flutter_lints defaults). |

208: | `GeneratedPluginRegistrant.*`, `generated_plugins.cmake` | Flutter tool, from declared plugins. |

| POST | `/projects/{id}/assign-owner` | admin | Set the project owner (must be active). |
| GET | `/members` | logged in, role-scoped | Admin: all; owner/user: own project only. |
| POST | `/members` | admin, owner | Create active member (role restricted per caller). |
| POST | `/members/{id}/confirm` | owner of that project, admin | Approve a pending join. |
| POST | `/members/{id}/role` | admin | Change a member's role. |
| GET | `/tasks?project_id=` or `?assignee_id=` | logged in, scoped | Exactly one filter required. |
| POST | `/tasks` | project members | Assignment rule enforced server-side. |
| PATCH | `/tasks/{id}` | project members | Partial edit: title, description, priority, due date, assignee. |
| PATCH | `/tasks/{id}/complete` / `/reopen` | project members | Status transitions. |

1: // Pure-Dart business rules. No Flutter, no database: unit-testable in isolation.
2: //
3: // Mirrors PROJECT_BRIEF.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md. The services
4: // in `lib/services/` enforce these rules against real rows; the checks here
5: // are the single definition of each rule.
6: 
7: // Roles (cumulative: admin > project owner > user).
8: abstract final class Roles {
9:   static const admin = 'admin';
10:   static const projectOwner = 'project_owner';
11:   static const user = 'user';
12: }
13: 
14: // Membership states.
15: abstract final class MemberStatus {
16:   static const pending = 'pending';
17:   static const active = 'active';
18: }
19: 
20: // Task states.
21: abstract final class TaskStatus {
22:   static const todo = 'todo';
23:   static const completed = 'completed';
24: }
25: 
26: /// A task is assigned either to its project as a whole ([assigneeId] null)
27: /// or to exactly one person, who must belong to the task's project.
28: void validateTaskAssignment({
29:   required int taskProjectId,
30:   required int? assigneeId,
31:   required int? assigneeProjectId,
32: }) {
33:   if (assigneeId != null && assigneeProjectId != taskProjectId) {
34:     throw ArgumentError('Assignee must belong to the task project.');
35:   }
36: }
37: 
38: /// Only active accounts may log in. Pending accounts wait for owner approval.
39: bool canLogIn(String status) => status == MemberStatus.active;
40: 
41: bool isAdmin(String role) => role == Roles.admin;
42: 
43: bool isOwnerOrAdmin(String role) =>
44:     role == Roles.admin || role == Roles.projectOwner;
45: 
46: /// Tabs visible for a role, in display order.
47: ///
48: /// Admins have no personal task list (they cannot be assignees); the
49: /// "mine" tab is for project owners and users.
50: List<String> visibleTabs(String role) {
51:   if (isAdmin(role)) {
52:     return const ['projects', 'members', 'tasks'];
53:   }
54:   return const ['members', 'tasks', 'mine'];
55: }
56: 
57: /// Throws [StateError] unless [role] is admin.
58: void requireAdmin(String role) {
59:   if (!isAdmin(role)) {
60:     throw StateError('Only an admin can do this.');
61:   }
62: }
63:

"""Task operations with server-enforced assignment and access rules."""
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from ..core.errors import ForbiddenError, NotFoundError, RuleError
from ..core.time import utc_now
from ..core.rules import (
    TASK_COMPLETED,
    TASK_TODO,
    can_log_in,
    is_admin,
    require_project_access,
    validate_task_assignment,
)
from ..models import Assignee, Project, Task


def list_tasks(
    db: Session,
    *,
    actor: Assignee,
    project_id: int | None,
    assignee_id: int | None,
) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks of one project or of one assignee, newest first."""
    if (project_id is None) == (assignee_id is None):
        raise RuleError("Provide project_id or assignee_id.")
    if project_id is not None:
        if not is_admin(actor.role) and actor.project_id != project_id:
            raise ForbiddenError("You can only view your own project tasks.")
        query = select(Task).where(Task.project_id == project_id)
    else:
        target = db.get(Assignee, assignee_id)
        if target is None:
            raise NotFoundError("Account not found.")
        if not is_admin(actor.role) and (
            actor.project_id is None or target.project_id != actor.project_id
        ):
            raise ForbiddenError(
                "You can only view your own project members' tasks."
            )
        query = select(Task).where(Task.assignee_id == assignee_id)
    return list(db.scalars(query.order_by(Task.created_at.desc())).all())


def create_task(
    db: Session,
    *,
    actor: Assignee,
    project_id: int,
    title: str,
    description: str | None,
    priority: str,
    due_date: date | None,
    assignee_id: int | None,
) -> Task:
    require_project_access(actor.role, actor.project_id, project_id)
    if db.get(Project, project_id) is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")
    if assignee_id is not None:
        assignee = db.get(Assignee, assignee_id)
        if assignee is None:
            raise NotFoundError("Account not found.")
        if not can_log_in(assignee.status):
            raise RuleError("Tasks can only be assigned to active members.")
        validate_task_assignment(
            task_project_id=project_id,
            assignee_id=assignee_id,
            assignee_project_id=assignee.project_id,
        )
    task = Task(
        title=title,
        description=description,
        priority=priority,
        due_date=due_date,
        project_id=project_id,
        assignee_id=assignee_id,
    )
    db.add(task)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(task)
    return task


def update_task(
    db: Session,
    *,
    actor: Assignee,
    task_id: int,
    changes: dict[str, Any],
) -> Task:
    """Apply a partial update; null clears optional fields.

    The project never changes here, so the same access rule as every other
    task mutation applies. Reassignment validates the new person just like
    creation does.
    """
    if not changes:
        raise RuleError("Nothing to update.")
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    if "title" in changes:
        if changes["title"] is None:
            raise RuleError("Title is required.")
        task.title = changes["title"]
    if "description" in changes:
        task.description = changes["description"]
    if "priority" in changes:
        if changes["priority"] is not None:
            task.priority = changes["priority"]
    if "due_date" in changes:
        task.due_date = changes["due_date"]
    if "assignee_id" in changes:
        assignee_id = changes["assignee_id"]
        if assignee_id is not None:
            assignee = db.get(Assignee, assignee_id)
            if assignee is None:
                raise NotFoundError("Account not found.")
            if not can_log_in(assignee.status):
                raise RuleError("Tasks can only be assigned to active members.")
            validate_task_assignment(
                task_project_id=task.project_id,
                assignee_id=assignee_id,
                assignee_project_id=assignee.project_id,
            )
        task.assignee_id = assignee_id
    task.updated_at = utc_now()
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(task)
    return task


def _load_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    task = db.get(Task, task_id)
    if task is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Task not found.")
    require_project_access(actor.role, actor.project_id, task.project_id)
    return task


def complete_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    now = utc_now()
    task.status = TASK_COMPLETED
    task.completed_at = now
    task.updated_at = now
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(task)
    return task


def reopen_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    task.status = TASK_TODO
    task.completed_at = None
    task.updated_at = utc_now()
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(task)
    return task


def delete_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> None:
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    db.delete(task)
    db.commit()

We are in Plan mode. User asks: "ya beaucoup des echecs pourquoi ? comment on peut les corrigent?" Need explain causes and propose fixes, no file changes. We have test results and code. Need analyze root causes deeply and propose correction plan, module by module, with priorities. We can inspect more to be accurate: failing tests, app code. We already read many. Need perhaps determine exact causes for Flutter failures. Let's analyze each failure thoroughly and propose fixes. This is a planning/diagnosis question, so we can discuss. No file modifications.

We should answer in French, clear and structured. Need likely inspect remaining code: task form dropdown, project card menu, member dialog, test harness, Flutter 3.47 behavior, data_sync test. We can reason and perhaps run targeted experiments? In Plan mode, can we run tests? Plan restrictions: do not modify files; running tests is read-only mostly but may write temp/build. It says "Do not modify any other files or ask a subagent to do so." Running tests could create temp files, but plan mode generally allows read-only exploration; earlier we ran tests while not in plan mode. Now in Plan mode, avoid modifying repo; running tests may be okay but perhaps not necessary. We have enough evidence. But to give precise causes, we may inspect test failure details and code.

Let's analyze each of the 9 failures (1 backend + 8 Flutter):

Backend `test_task_list_is_newest_first`:
- `list_tasks` orders by `Task.created_at.desc()`.
- MySQL `DateTime` default has second precision (no fractional seconds). Three tasks created within same second get identical `created_at` values, so order is unspecified; InnoDB likely returns primary key ascending. Thus oldest first. Fix options:
  1. Order by `Task.created_at.desc(), Task.id.desc()` ÔÇö deterministic newest-first, minimal.
  2. Store microseconds (`DateTime(6)` / `func.now(6)`) ÔÇö migration + model change; more accurate but heavier.
  3. In tests, add delay >1s ÔÇö hides bug; not recommended.
- Recommendation: add secondary sort by id desc. Need approval because behavior/DB query change. Also update test maybe not needed; it will pass.
- Potential other endpoints sorting? `list_members` by name; projects by name. Only tasks.

Flutter failures:
1 & 2 & 3: Popup menu taps "Log out" / "Bob Builder" not hit-testable. Warning says offset outside hit test, hit result contains `RenderIgnorePointer`/`RenderAbsorbPointer`, `_RenderTheater` overlay. Likely the menu overlay animation hasn't finished or test surface / menu positioning. In tests, they tap menu button, then `tester.pump(Duration(milliseconds: 300))`, then tap text. On current Flutter, popup menu opens with animation ~300ms; one pump of 300ms advances animation but maybe not a zero-duration frame to settle. `pump` advances clock and draws one frame at end; might still need `pumpAndSettle` or an extra pump. The `NEEDS-PAINT` suggests render object not painted; possibly because the menu is still animating/opacity 0. The hit test result `RenderIgnorePointer` likely from modal barrier, and text is behind it? If menu is still in route transition, ignore pointer is active. Fix test: use `await tester.pumpAndSettle()` after opening popup, or `await settle(tester)` (8 frames ├ù 100ms) before tapping. Or use `tester.tap(find.byType(PopupMenuItem<String>).last)`? The actual menu item might be hit. Better use `pumpAndSettle` and `warnIfMissed: false`? Don't hide.
- Could there be an actual app issue? On a real device, menus work; tests only. The warning says tap point 609,104 outside screen? Wait offset 609,104; screen likely 800x600; inside. But hit test returns overlay perhaps menu barrier. Hmm. The test taps `find.text('Log out')` but the text widget's global position is offset; maybe because the popup menu item is in an overlay outside the main Navigator? `find.text` finds it, but at that point it's not hit-testable due to `IgnorePointer` during route transition. So timing.
- In `projects_tab_test`, tapping "Bob Builder" maybe picks text in the project card background (owner candidate?) rather than menu item; warning says "ignoring all but last", but there may be duplicate text: current owner "Olive Owner" and candidate "Bob Builder" only menu. The hit result includes overlay barrier. Timing likely.
- Fix: tests use `pumpAndSettle` after opening menus; possibly also ensure `find.text(...).last` hit target. Could define helper `openPopupAndTap`. That's test-only change.
- Alternative product fix: use `PopupMenuButton.onSelected` and test via semantics? Not needed.

4. Projects empty/error test:
- Test starts with empty projects, then sets `api.projectsError = 'offline'`, taps Tasks tab, expects "Could not load projects". But TasksTab for admin watches `projectsProvider`; the provider was already loaded successfully with empty list at app startup (Projects tab? Actually admin lands on Projects tab, projectsProvider invoked and returns empty). Switching to Tasks reuses cached value; it does not refetch because no invalidation. So no error. The test assumption is wrong, or the app should refetch on tab switch/error scenario. Behavior in real app: if API goes down after initial load, list remains cached until refresh; that's acceptable. Test should use a fresh app with `projectsError` set before pumping, or invalidate provider. Fix test setup: set `api.projectsError` before `pumpTaskPlanner` for the error phase, or use a separate test. Could also add pull-to-refresh; but not necessary. This is a test design issue.
- Also the test expects "No project available" after retry with empty list; TasksTab shows "No project available." if no projects. That likely works.

5. Members add user:
- Test taps FAB 'Add user', then pumps 300ms, then enters text. `_addDialog` awaits `ref.read(projectsProvider.future)` before showing dialog. Even though projectsProvider may be loaded, for an owner it wasn't watched (owner lands on Members, no Projects tab), so it starts a stream/future. The future resolves via FakeApiClient but requires an event-loop turn; 300ms pump should process? Maybe not because `_addDialog` is async and `projectsProvider.future` resolves after a microtask, but `pump` may not flush it before dialog shown? It should. However, test shows only one TextField (search field), so dialog not shown. Could be because `projectsProvider.future` never completes due to StreamProvider behavior: `ref.read(projectsProvider.future)` starts the provider, but since not watched (no listener), Riverpod may auto-dispose after first read or not execute? In Riverpod 3, reading `.future` creates a temporary subscription; it should. But maybe `projectsProvider` is already in `AsyncLoading` and no listener, so it doesn't run? Hmm. More likely test timing.
- The fix: in the test, use `await settle(tester)` after tapping FAB (not just `pump(300ms)`), and perhaps wait for dialog title. Or app improvement: don't await projects for owner (owner doesn't need project list; only admin does). `_addDialog` currently always fetches projects, even for owner, though AddMemberDialog uses projects only if admin. That's an unnecessary API call and can block the dialog if projects fail. For an owner, it could open immediately with empty projects. This is a real UX/robustness issue: owner adding a member depends on `/projects` being reachable, even though it only needs own project. Fix app: only fetch projects when `isAdmin(viewer.role)`, else pass `const []`; show dialog immediately. This would also make test pass if timing. Good insight. This is an app change (behavior) requiring approval. It also aligns with "owner add user" not needing project stream.
- Alternatively test adjust pump. But better fix app minimal.

6. Tasks create:
- Test opens add task dialog, taps Create with empty title -> error; enters title; taps priority dropdown, selects High; taps assignee dropdown, selects Bob; taps Create; expects task in fake API. It gets none. Could be dropdown interactions not selecting due to overlay/timing; same overlay issue: `tester.pump(300ms)` after each dropdown, then `tester.tap(find.text('High').last)`. Popup menus may not be fully open/hit-testable, so selection not registered. Then Create maybe not hit? It likely creates with default priority/assignee? But `fixture.api.tasks` empty means Create didn't happen or form validation failed (title maybe not entered due to focus?).
- Need inspect TaskFormDialog and test. The dropdown is `DropdownButtonFormField<String>` and `DropdownButtonFormField<int?>`. Tapping opens menu; `pump(300)` maybe not enough. Use `pumpAndSettle`.
- Another possible bug: `DropdownButtonFormField<int?>` with a `DropdownMenuItem` without `value` (null) and `initialValue: null`; selecting Bob value 3 should work. But the menu items include all visible members; for user Bob, `_membersFor` filters to project and includes Bob. Could be fine.
- The test expects `fixture.api.tasks.single` immediately after `settle`; fake API `_createTask` may require actor role/project; user Bob is active and project member; should create. If dropdown tap missed but Create still tapped, default medium/whole project would create a task; tasks would not be empty. Since empty, Create likely not submitted (maybe dialog still open due to dropdown route overlay; tap on Create missed). So timing/overlay.
- Fix tests with `pumpAndSettle` after dropdown opens; perhaps use `tester.tap(find.text('High').last)` then `pumpAndSettle`. Also ensure dialog is open using `find.text('New task')`.
- App could improve by using `DropdownMenu` or making dropdown selection easier, but no need.

7. Tasks grouping missing "No due date":
- `TaskList` uses `ListView.builder` with rows for sections; only visible items are built. Test expects all five headers without scrolling. In current viewport, "Overdue", "Today", "Upcoming" fit, "No due date" and "Completed" are below; finder can't find unbuilt widgets. Fix test: use `scrollUntilVisible` for each header, or set a larger test surface (`tester.view.physicalSize`/`devicePixelRatio`), or use `find.text` after scrolling. Could also change UI to `ListView` with all children (less efficient; not recommended). Test-only fix.
- Alternatively test can assert `find.text('No due date', skipOffstage: false)` won't work if not built. Scroll.
- This is not an app bug.

8. Data sync test timeout:
- Need deeper analysis. The test uses `service.watchProjectTasks(...).listen`, delays 20ms, expects [0], creates task, delays 20ms, expects [0,1]. It times out after 30s. Where exactly? The test may hang at `await service.createTask(...)`? FakeApiClient `_createTask` maybe calls `DataSync.instance.ping()`? Let's inspect `_createTask` rest of fake API.

# Skill: flutter-ui

# Flutter UI

Approved stack: Flutter/Dart, Riverpod for state and DI, go_router for navigation. Approved layer-first layout: `lib/app/`, `lib/core/`, `lib/models/`, `lib/providers/`, `lib/screens/`, `lib/services/`, `lib/widgets/`. Create only folders needed for approved features.

## Rules

- Screens and widgets display state and forward user actions to the application layer. No business rules in UI code.
- UI code must never call the API, the database, or `HttpApiClient` directly; it goes through providers and services (see `database-design` for the model).
- Reuse `lib/core/` theme and shared utilities plus `lib/widgets/shared/`; do not duplicate styling per screen.
- Navigation changes go through `lib/app/router.dart`; do not hard-code route strings in widgets.
- New screens or navigation structure are application-behavior changes: propose and wait for approval (see `interactive-development`).

## UX direction (from the brief)

On open, the user must quickly see what is due today, what is overdue, what is most important, and what is completed. Avoid unnecessary screens and complicated workflows.

The app opens on a login page with a link to the sign-up page. Auth screens collect credentials only; all role and membership checks happen in the application layer, never in widgets.

## Screen order

1. **Login page** ÔÇö the app's start screen, always shown first; links to sign-up.
2. **Sign-up page** ÔÇö reachable only from login (name, email, password, project choice).
3. **Role tabs, only after successful login** ÔÇö Projects (admin only ÔÇö create, list, assign owners), Members (all roles, scoped roster; pending-requests section for owner/admin), Tasks (all roles, scoped), Mine (owner and user ÔÇö tasks assigned to the logged-in person; not admin).

No route may render before authentication completes: deep links and restarts land on the login page first.

The definitive per-role mapping lives in the `access-control` skill; keep this list in sync with it.

Which tabs each role sees and how data is scoped per role is defined in the `access-control` skill ÔÇö implement that mapping here without redefining it.

<skill_content name="database-design">
# Skill: database-design

# Database Design

Source of truth for the model: PROJECT_BRIEF.md (Task Assignment, Assignee Management) and docs/ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md ┬º8. The model below is implemented on the server (`backend/app/models/`, `backend/app/schemas/`).

## Current model (implemented)

- `projects`: id, name, optional description, status (active/archived), `owner_id` (assigned by an admin), created_at.
- `assignees`: id, name, position (job title, display only ÔÇö not the access role), `project_id` (each person belongs to exactly one project; admins act across all projects), email (unique login), password_hash (salted), role (admin/project_owner/user, cumulative), status (pending/active), `approved_by` (confirming owner's id, null until confirmed), created_at.
- `tasks`: id, title (required), optional description, status (to do/completed), priority (low/medium/high), optional due_date, `project_id` (required), `assignee_id` (optional), created_at, updated_at, completed_at.

## Assignment rules

- A task belongs to a project and has at most one assignee: the project as a whole (`assignee_id` NULL ÔÇö several people affected) or exactly one person (`assignee_id` set). Never both.
- A person assignee must belong to the task's project. Enforce this in the application/business-logic layer, not just the UI.
- Assigning a task to a project other than its own is out of scope unless approved.

## Access rules

See the `access-control` skill for roles, capabilities, membership approval, and enforcement. This skill owns the tables and columns; `access-control` owns who may do what.

## Constraints

- Online-only: task data requires the FastAPI API (`/api/v1`); offline sync is out of scope.
- MySQL stores all data; the server is the single enforcement point for roles, approval, and assignment rules.
- UI code must never access the API or database directly; business rules must be testable without the UI.
- Schema changes go through Alembic (`backend/alembic/`); dev startup may create missing tables only in development.
- Changing the model, tables, or persistence approach requires a proposal and explicit approval (see `interactive-development`, AGENTS.md approval requirements).

const BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:60074';
export async function connect() {
  const targets = await (await fetch(BASE + '/json/list')).json();
  const page = targets.find(t => t.type === 'page' && t.url.includes('63787')) || targets.find(t => t.type === 'page');
  const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
  await new Promise((res, rej) => { ws.onopen = res; ws.onerror = rej; });
  let id = 0; const pending = new Map();
  ws.onmessage = (ev) => { const msg = JSON.parse(ev.data); if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) { const {resolve, reject} = pending.get(msg.id); pending.delete(msg.id); msg.error ? reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error))) : resolve(msg.result); } };
  const send = (method, params={}) => new Promise((resolve, reject) => { const mid = ++id; pending.set(mid, {resolve, reject}); ws.send(JSON.stringify({id: mid, method, params})); });
  return { send, ws, page };
}

- Visible Chrome automation became unreliable (semantics crash, screenshot hang); E2E now runs in headless Chrome on CDP port `60075`.

# Skill: interactive-development

# Interactive Development

The workflow for every meaningful change. AGENTS.md holds the binding rules; this skill holds the procedure.

**Step 1 ÔÇö Inspect.** Read AGENTS.md, PROJECT_BRIEF.md, and relevant docs. Inspect existing files, find reusable code and tests. Do not assume the repository is empty.

**Step 2 ÔÇö Understand.** Identify the intended user outcome, the relevant business rules, missing information, and conflicting requirements. State assumptions explicitly.

**Step 3 ÔÇö Propose.** Before changing files, describe the problem, the solution, the files that would change, new dependencies or architectural impact, and how it will be tested.

**Step 4 ÔÇö Stop and wait.** Request explicit approval. Do not implement until approval is received. Architectural changes need a new proposal even when discovered mid-implementation.

**Step 5 ÔÇö Implement minimally.** Make only the approved changes. Reuse existing utilities and patterns. No unrelated refactoring, no silent scope expansion.

**Step 6 ÔÇö Verify.** Run relevant tests and checks, inspect the changes, report actual results and unresolved failures. Never invent test results.

**Step 7 ÔÇö Record and stop.** Update relevant documentation, report what changed and what remains, then stop and wait.

## Which domain skill to load

- Data model, schema, persistence, repositories, migrations ÔåÆ `database-design`
- Roles, permissions, join approval, who-can-do-what ÔåÆ `access-control`
- Screens, widgets, navigation, theming, UI state ÔåÆ `flutter-ui`
- Writing or running tests, verifying changes ÔåÆ `testing-and-verification`
- Updating docs or recording a decision ÔåÆ `documentation-and-decisions`

# Skill: access-control

# Access Control

Source of truth: PROJECT_BRIEF.md (┬º5 rules, Accounts and Roles) and docs/ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md ┬º8. Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/2026-10-11-local-auth-and-roles.md`.

## Roles

Three cumulative roles: an admin can do everything a project owner and a user can do; a project owner everything a user can do.

- **Admin** ÔÇö owns the system: creates projects, assigns project owners, creates users anywhere, manages roles, confirms any join request, and sees every tab and all data.
- **Project owner** ÔÇö owns their projects: confirms or rejects join requests, sees all members and their statuses (pending/active), manages tasks and assignments, creates users inside their own projects. No project creation, no role changes.
- **User** ÔÇö works their tasks: views and completes assigned tasks, manages tasks in their own project. Must sign up and be confirmed before first login.

## Capability matrix

| Capability | User | Project Owner | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Log in (active accounts only) | Ô£ô | Ô£ô | Ô£ô |
| View and complete assigned tasks | own project | own projects | all projects |
| Create, edit, delete tasks | own project | own projects | all projects |
| Assign tasks to the project or a person | ÔÇö | own projects | all projects |
| Confirm or reject join requests | ÔÇö | own projects | all projects |
| Create users (role user) | ÔÇö | own projects | anywhere |
| Create projects, assign owners, manage roles | ÔÇö | ÔÇö | Ô£ô |

## Workflows

**New user (self-registration).** Open app ÔåÆ sign-up page (name, email, password, choose project) ÔåÆ account created as pending ÔåÆ relevant project owner confirms ÔåÆ user logs in ÔåÆ sees today's tasks. Pending users cannot log in.

**Project owner (enrollment).** Log in ÔåÆ Members tab ÔåÆ pending-requests section lists everyone waiting for their projects ÔåÆ confirm or reject ÔåÆ member becomes active and can log in. Roster shows every member with pending/active status.

**Admin (setup).** Log in ÔåÆ Projects tab ÔåÆ create project ÔåÆ assign its owner ÔåÆ optionally create users directly (active immediately). Can open every tab across all projects.

## Tabs per role (approved 2026-10-18)

- **Projects** ÔÇö admin only: create projects, list all, assign owners.
- **Members** ÔÇö all roles, scoped: user sees their own project's roster; owner sees their projects' rosters with pending/active statuses plus the pending-requests section; admin sees everyone including roles.
- **Tasks** ÔÇö all roles, scoped: user sees own project's tasks; owner their projects'; admin all.
- **Mine** ÔÇö owner and user (not admin, who can never be an assignee): tasks assigned to the logged-in person only (`assignee_id` = viewer), enforced by `TaskService.watchTasksAssignedTo`.
- **Approvals** live inside the Members tab as the pending-requests section (owner/admin only), not as a separate tab ÔÇö the brief asks for minimal screens.

Tab changes are business-rule changes; record them under `docs/decisions/`.

## Data scoping

Everyone sees only their own projects' data ÔÇö tasks, members, and requests are always filtered to the viewer's project(s). Only admins bypass the filter. Scoping is enforced in the application layer, not just by hiding tabs.

## Membership lifecycle

- Admins and project owners create active users directly.
- Self-registered users start as pending and cannot log in until the relevant project owner (or an admin) confirms them; confirmation records the owner's id in `approved_by`.
- Credentials live only in the local person table; passwords are salted hashes, never plain text.
- Key events raise an email notification through the device's mail app (proposed): a new sign-up notifies the project owner, approval or rejection notifies the user, a new assignment notifies the assignee.

## Enforcement

- Role, scope, and membership checks belong in the application/business-logic layer. The UI may hide actions, but must never be the only check.
- Changing roles, the matrix, workflows, tabs, or the approval flow is a business-rule change: propose and wait for approval (see `interactive-development`).

# Automatic Logout on an Authenticated 401

- Date: 2026-10-25
- Status: approved and implemented (user approved automatic logout with a
  message)
- Context: E2E E8 and gap G2. When the API rejected an authenticated request
  with 401, the UI stayed on `/home` with `Invalid or expired token` and a Retry
  button. A genuinely expired token could never recover, so the user was stuck
  until a manual logout ÔÇö with no indication that the session was over.
- Options considered:
  1. **End the session and return to login with a notice (chosen)** ÔÇö matches
     the meaning of 401, keeps the user in control, no API change.
  2. Keep the error screen with Retry ÔÇö rejected: no request can succeed with an
     invalid token, so Retry is a dead end.
  3. Silent logout without a message ÔÇö rejected: the sudden return to login
     looks like data loss or a bug.
  4. Refresh-token flow ÔÇö rejected for now: the API issues no refresh token and
     adding one changes the contract.
- Decision:
  - `ApiClient` exposes `setUnauthorizedHandler`; `HttpApiClient` remembers
    whether a token was attached to the request and invokes the handler on 401;
  - 401 responses without a token (login, sign-up) never invoke it, so a wrong
    password keeps its normal `Wrong email or password.` message;
  - the handler clears the token, closes the session, shows
    `Your session expired. Log in again.` on the login screen and lets the
    router redirect;
  - state changes are deferred to a microtask because the callback runs while a
    provider is building and Riverpod forbids modifying another provider during
    initialization;
  - the notice is cleared on the next login attempt and on a normal logout.
- Implementation:
  - `task_planner/lib/services/api_client.dart` ÔÇö handler and token-aware 401;
  - `task_planner/lib/app/app.dart` ÔÇö wiring, token/session cleanup, microtask;
  - `task_planner/lib/providers/session_providers.dart` ÔÇö
    `sessionNoticeProvider`;
  - `task_planner/lib/screens/login_screen.dart` ÔÇö notice banner;
  - `task_planner/test/support/fake_api_client.dart` ÔÇö `unauthorized` mode;
  - `task_planner/test/api_client_test.dart` ÔÇö 2 unit tests (authenticated 401
    notifies, tokenless 401 does not);
  - `task_planner/test/session_expiry_test.dart` ÔÇö 2 widget tests (expiry then
    successful re-login).
- Verification:
  - `flutter analyze --no-pub`: clean; targeted files 23/23; full suite 69/69;
  - backend pytest: 59/59 (no API change);
  - E8 replayed on the real stack: the API was recreated with a different
    `SECRET_KEY`, an authenticated request from the Tasks tab returned 401, the
    app landed on `/#/login` with the notice and rendered no member/project
    data; a wrong-password attempt showed only the credential error; after the
    original secret was restored, a full login succeeded ÔÇö **PASS**. Evidence:
    `01-e8c-expired-login`, `02-e8c-wrong-password`,
    `01-e8d-recovered-login` in `%TEMP%\opencode\e2e\`.
- Consequences:
  - manual logout still works and clears the notice;
  - the token remains memory-only: reloading or restarting still returns to
    login (G5, unchanged and still open).

2: 
3: > **Amended 2026-10-21:** the approved build uses a FastAPI + MySQL backend and

8: ## 1. Project Goal
9: 
10: Build a task planner mobile application that helps the user organize tasks and decide what to work on next.
11: 
12: The app should be simple, reliable, easy to use, and usable without an internet connection.
13: 
14: ## 2. Target Platform
15: 
16: - Mobile application built with Flutter and Dart.
17: - Android is the initial target.
18: - Keep the architecture open to supporting iOS later.
19: 
20: ## 3. First Release (MVP)
21: 
22: The first release should focus on essential task management:
23: 
24: - Create a task.
25: - Edit a task.
26: - Delete a task.
27: - Mark a task as completed.
28: - Reopen a completed task.
29: - Assign a priority.
30: - Optionally set a due date.
31: - View today's tasks.
32: - View upcoming and overdue tasks.
33: - Save tasks locally so they remain available after closing and reopening the app.
34: - Log in with an account (login page).
35: - Create an account (sign-up page).
36: 
37: ## 4. Initial User Experience
38: 
39: The user should be able to open the app and quickly understand:
40: 
41: - What needs to be done today.
42: - Which tasks are overdue.
43: - Which tasks are most important.
44: - What has already been completed.
45: 
46: Avoid unnecessary screens and complicated workflows.
47: 
48: The app opens on a login page; new users reach the sign-up page from there.
49: 
50: ## 5. Business Rules
51: 
52: - A task must have a title.
53: - A task is not required to have a due date.
54: - New tasks are incomplete by default.
55: - Completing a task records when it was completed.
56: - Reopening a task clears its completion timestamp.
57: - An incomplete task is overdue when its due date has passed.
58: - Completed tasks are not considered overdue.
59: - Task data must persist locally.
60: - Using the app requires an account; accounts are stored locally on the device.
61: - Login uses a unique email and a password (stored as a salted hash, never plain text).
62: - A self-registered account stays pending and cannot log in until the relevant project owner confirms it.
63: - Approval records the confirming project owner's id (`approved_by`).
64: - Roles are admin, project owner, and user, and they are cumulative: an admin can do everything a project owner and a user can do, and a project owner everything a user can do.
65: - Only an admin creates projects, assigns project owners, and manages roles.
66: - A project owner confirms new members of their own project and manages its tasks and assignments.
67: 
68: ## 6. Constraints
69: 
70: - Offline-first: core functionality must work without internet access.
71: - Multiple user accounts stored locally on a single device; no backend server is required for the initial version.
72: - Keep the implementation simple and maintainable.
73: - Avoid unnecessary dependencies and architectural complexity.
74: - Do not introduce AI features until the core task planner works reliably.
75: 
76: ## 7. Decisions Not Yet Finalized
77: 
78: The following require discussion before implementation:
79: 
80: - Whether tasks should also support categories alongside projects.
81: - Whether reminders and notifications belong in the first release.
82: - Whether the app needs manual backup and restore.
83: - Whether the main planner should show a daily view, weekly view, or both.
84: - Which priority levels and task statuses are needed.
85: - The final architecture, database, and state-management choices.
86: - How the very first admin account is created on a fresh install.
87: - Password recovery or reset without a backend (for example, admin resets passwords).
88: - Which events trigger email notifications (proposed: new sign-up, approval or rejection, task assignment).
89: 
90: Do not silently decide these questions if they materially affect the design.
91: 
92: ## 8. Development Rules
93: 
94: - Inspect the existing repository before proposing changes.
95: - Reuse existing code and project conventions where appropriate.
96: - Propose architectural changes and wait for explicit approval.
97: - Do not implement unapproved features or install dependencies without approval.
98: - Keep changes small and test them independently.
99: - Report what was changed, what was tested, and any remaining issues.
100: 
101: ## 9. Initial Development Objective
102: 
103: Start with discovery, not implementation.
104: 
105: Review this brief alongside the repository and proposed architecture. Identify missing requirements, important questions, risks, and the smallest useful next step.
106: 
107: Do not modify files or write application code during discovery. Present recommendations and wait for approval.
108: 
109: ## Task Assignment
110: 
111: Each task has at most one assignee.
112: 
113: The assignee can be either:
114: 
115: - **A person** ÔÇö identified by name, with a position such as Developer, Project Manager, or Business Analyst. Exactly one person is responsible.
116: - **A project** ÔÇö the task is assigned to the project as a whole, meaning several people are affected; no single person is named.
117: 
118: Task rules:
119: 
120: - A task belongs to a project.
121: - A task can be assigned to that project as a whole (no individual assignee) or to one person from the project ÔÇö never both at the same time.
122: - A person assignee must belong to the task's project.
123: - The assignee's position should be available when viewing the task.
124: - The assignee should be optional unless the user decides otherwise.
125: - The app should support assigning tasks to different people, not only the current user.
126: 
127: ## Assignee Management
128: 
129: The application should provide a way to manage assignee information so the same person does not need to be entered from scratch for every task.
130: 
131: The exact management interface and data model must be proposed before implementation.
132: 
133: Each assignee belongs to a project via a `project_id` foreign key.
134: 
135: ## Accounts and Roles
136: 
137: - The app opens on a login page; a sign-up page creates a new account.
138: - An admin creates each project and assigns its project owner.
139: - New users are created by an admin, by a project owner, or by self-registration.
140: - Approval records which project owner confirmed the account.

def bulk_complete_tasks(
    db: Session,
    *,
    actor: Assignee,
    task_ids: list[int],
) -> BulkTaskResultOut:
    """Bulk complete multiple tasks (actor must have mutate access to each)."""
    results: list[BulkTaskResult] = []
    for tid in task_ids:
        try:
            complete_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=tid)
            results.append(BulkTaskResult(task_id=tid, success=True))
        except Exception as e:
            results.append(BulkTaskResult(task_id=tid, success=False, error=str(e)))
    return BulkTaskResultOut(
        results=results,
        total=len(results),
        succeeded=sum(1 for r in results if r.success),
        failed=sum(1 for r in results if not r.success),
    )

def update_task(
    db: Session,
    *,
    actor: Assignee,
    task_id: int,
    changes: dict[str, Any],
) -> Task:
    """Apply a partial update; null clears optional fields.

    The project never changes here, so the same access rule as every other
    task mutation applies. Reassignment validates the new person just like
    creation does.
    """
    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    if not changes:
        raise RuleError("Nothing to update.")
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    previous_assignee_id = task.assignee_id
    if "title" in changes:
        if changes["title"] is None:
            raise RuleError("Title is required.")
        task.title = changes["title"]
    if "description" in changes:
        task.description = changes["description"]
    if "priority" in changes:
        if changes["priority"] is not None:
            task.priority = changes["priority"]
    if "due_date" in changes:
        task.due_date = changes["due_date"]
    if "assignee_id" in changes:
        assignee_id = changes["assignee_id"]
        if assignee_id is not None:
            assignee = db.get(Assignee, assignee_id)
            if assignee is None:
                raise NotFoundError("Account not found.")
            if not can_log_in(assignee.status):
                raise RuleError("Tasks can only be assigned to active members.")
            validate_task_assignment(
                task_project_id=task.project_id,
                assignee_id=assignee_id,
                assignee_project_id=assignee.project_id,
            )
        task.assignee_id = assignee_id
    task.updated_at = utc_now()
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(task)
    # Notify when the assignee changed.
    if (
        task.assignee_id is not None
        and task.assignee_id != previous_assignee_id
    ):
        target = db.get(Assignee, task.assignee_id)
        project = db.get(Project, task.project_id)
        notification_service.notify_task_assigned(
            db,
            task=task,
            actor=actor,
            project_name=project.name if project else "",
            assignee=target,
            previous_assignee_id=previous_assignee_id,
        )
        analytics_service.record_event(
            db,
            project_id=task.project_id,
            actor_id=actor.id,
            event_type="task_assigned",
            task_id=task.id,
        )
        db.commit()
    return task


def _load_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    task = db.get(Task, task_id)
    if task is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Task not found.")
    require_project_access(actor.role, actor.project_id, task.project_id)
    return task


def complete_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    now = utc_now()
    task.status = TASK_COMPLETED
    task.completed_at = now
    task.updated_at = now
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(task)
    # Notify the assignee (if different from the actor).
    if task.assignee_id is not None and task.assignee_id != actor.id:
        target = db.get(Assignee, task.assignee_id)
        project = db.get(Project, task.project_id)
        notification_service.notify_task_completed(
            db,
            task=task,
            actor=actor,
            project_name=project.name if project else "",
            assignee=target,
        )
        analytics_service.record_event(
            db,
            project_id=task.project_id,
            actor_id=actor.id,
            event_type="task_completed",
            task_id=task.id,
        )
        db.commit()
    return task


def reopen_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    task = _load_task(db, actor=actor, task_id=task_id)
    task.status = TASK_TODO
    task.completed_at = None
    task.updated_at = utc_now()
    db.commit()

    if task.assignee_id is not None and task.assignee_id != actor.id:

def get_dashboard(db: Session, *, project_id: int) -> DashboardOut:
    """Compute dashboard metrics for one project."""
    project = db.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        from ..core.errors import NotFoundError

        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")

    now = utc_now()
    # All tasks of the project.
    tasks = list(
        db.scalars(select(Task).where(Task.project_id == project_id)).all()
    )
    total = len(tasks)
    completed = [t for t in tasks if t.status == "completed"]
    pending = [t for t in tasks if t.status != "completed"]

    # Overdue: incomplete + due_date < today.
    today = now.date()
    overdue = [
        t
        for t in pending
        if t.due_date is not None and t.due_date < today
    ]

    completion_rate = round((len(completed) / total * 100), 1) if total else 0.0
    overdue_rate = round((len(overdue) / total * 100), 1) if total else 0.0

    # Priority mix.
    priority_mix: dict[str, int] = {"low": 0, "medium": 0, "high": 0}
    for t in tasks:
        key = t.priority if t.priority in priority_mix else "medium"
        priority_mix[key] += 1

    # Velocity: completed tasks per week over the last 4 weeks.
    four_weeks_ago = now - timedelta(weeks=4)
    recent_completed = [
        t
        for t in completed
        if t.completed_at is not None
        and t.completed_at >= four_weeks_ago
    ]
    velocity_per_week = round(len(recent_completed) / 4.0, 1)

    # Recent events (last 20).
    recent_rows = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(AnalyticsEvent)
            .where(AnalyticsEvent.project_id == project_id)
            .order_by(AnalyticsEvent.created_at.desc(), AnalyticsEvent.id.desc())
            .limit(20)
        ).all()
    )
    actor_names: dict[int, str] = {}
    recent_events: list[DashboardEventOut] = []
    for ev in recent_rows:
        if ev.actor_id not in actor_names:
            actor = db.get(Assignee, ev.actor_id)
            actor_names[ev.actor_id] = actor.name if actor else "Unknown"
        recent_events.append(
            DashboardEventOut(
                id=ev.id,
                event_type=ev.event_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                task_id=ev.task_id,
                actor_id=ev.actor_id,
                actor_name=actor_names[ev.actor_id],
                created_at=ev.created_at,
            )
        )

    return DashboardOut(
        project_id=project.id,
        project_name=project.name,
        total_tasks=total,
        completed_tasks=len(completed),
        pending_tasks=len(pending),
        overdue_tasks=len(overdue),
        completion_rate=completion_rate,
        overdue_rate=overdue_rate,
        priority_mix=priority_mix,
        velocity_per_week=velocity_per_week,
        recent_events=recent_events,
    )

def _load_task(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, task_id: int) -> Task:
    task = db.get(Task, task_id)
    if task is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Task not found.")
    if not _can_access(actor.role, actor.project_id, task.project_id):
        raise ForbiddenError("You can only manage subtasks of your own project tasks.")
    return task


def _can_access(role: str, actor_project_id: int | None, task_project_id: int) -> bool:
    from ..core.rules import is_admin

    if is_admin(role):
        return True
    return actor_project_id is not None and actor_project_id == task_project_id

def confirm_member(
    db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, user_id: int
) -> Assignee:
    target = db.get(Assignee, user_id)
    if target is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Account not found.")
    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    if not is_admin(actor.role):
        if not (is_owner_or_admin(actor.role) or is_team_lead(actor.role)):
            raise ForbiddenError("Only admins, owners, and team leads can confirm members.")
        if actor.project_id is None or target.project_id != actor.project_id:
            raise ForbiddenError("You can only confirm your own project members.")
    target.status = ACTIVE
    target.approved_by = actor.id
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(target)
    # Notify the confirmed member (if confirmed by someone else).
    if target.id != actor.id:
        project = db.get(Project, target.project_id) if target.project_id else None
        notification_service.notify_member_confirmed(
            db,
            member=target,
            actor=actor,
            project_name=project.name if project else "",

        db.commit()
    return target

        notification_service.notify_member_role_changed(
            db,
            member=target,
            actor=actor,
            project_name=project.name if project else "",
            new_role=role,
        )
        db.commit()
    return target

def archive_project(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, project_id: int) -> Project:
    """Archive a project (admin only). Archiving hides it from default lists."""
    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    require_admin(actor.role)
    project = db.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")
    project.status = "archived"
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(project)
    return project


def restore_project(db: Session, *, actor: Assignee, project_id: int) -> Project:
    """Restore an archived project (admin only)."""
    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    require_admin(actor.role)
    project = db.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")
    project.status = "active"
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(project)
    return project

    description: str | None,

    require_admin(actor.role)

    db.commit()

    return project

"""In-app notifications + email delivery for task/member actions.

Each action creates a `Notification` row (so the mobile client can list them)
and, when the recipient has opted in, sends an email via `email_service`.
"""
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from ..core.config import SMTP_HOST
from ..core.time import utc_now
from ..models import Assignee, Notification, Task
from . import email_service


def _notify(
    db: Session,
    *,
    user: Assignee,
    n_type: str,
    title: str,
    body: str | None = None,
    payload: str | None = None,
    send_email: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Persist an in-app notification and optionally email the recipient."""
    db.add(
        Notification(
            user_id=user.id,
            type=n_type,
            title=title,
            body=body,
            payload=payload,
        )
    )
    db.flush()
    if send_email and email_service.is_configured() and user.email:
        email_service.send(
            to=user.email,
            subject=title,
            body=body or title,
        )


def notify_task_created(
    db: Session,
    *,
    task: Task,
    actor: Assignee,
    project_name: str,
    assignee: Assignee | None,
) -> None:
    """A task was created; notify its assignee (if any) and project members."""
    if assignee is not None and assignee.id != actor.id:
        _notify(
            db,
            user=assignee,
            n_type="task_created",
            title=f"New task assigned: {task.title}",
            body=(
                f"{actor.name} assigned you to '{task.title}' in project "
                f"'{project_name}'."
            ),
            payload=str(task.id),
        )

    # Email the whole project is out of scope for v1; only the assignee gets
    # a direct notification. Project-wide digest is deferred.


def notify_task_assigned(
    db: Session,
    *,
    task: Task,
    actor: Assignee,
    project_name: str,
    assignee: Assignee,
    previous_assignee_id: int | None,
) -> None:
    """A task's assignee changed; notify the new assignee."""
    if assignee.id == actor.id:
        return
    _notify(
        db,
        user=assignee,
        n_type="task_assigned",
        title=f"Task assigned to you: {task.title}",
        body=(
            f"{actor.name} assigned '{task.title}' to you in project "
            f"'{project_name}'."
        ),
        payload=str(task.id),
    )


def notify_task_completed(
    db: Session,
    *,
    task: Task,
    actor: Assignee,
    project_name: str,
    assignee: Assignee | None,
) -> None:
    """A task was completed; notify its assignee (if any)."""
    if assignee is None or assignee.id == actor.id:
        return
    _notify(
        db,
        user=assignee,
        n_type="task_completed",
        title=f"Task completed: {task.title}",
        body=(
            f"{actor.name} marked '{task.title}' as completed in project "
            f"'{project_name}'."
        ),
        payload=str(task.id),
    )


def notify_task_reopened(
    db: Session,
    *,
    task: Task,
