247: **Confirmed rules**:
248: - A task has at most one assignee target: the project or a person, never both
249: - A person assignee must belong to the same project as the task
250: - Each person belongs to exactly one project

253: - Only an admin creates projects and assigns project owners
254: - Only an admin creates owner/admin accounts or changes roles
255: - Admins and project owners create active users directly
256: - Self-registered users start as pending and cannot log in until confirmed

    if not is_admin(actor.role):
        if actor.project_id is None:
            raise RuleError("Account has not been assigned to a project.")
        query = query.where(Assignee.project_id == actor.project_id)
    total = db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(query.subquery()))
    items = list(db.scalars(query.limit(limit).offset(offset)).all())
    return items, total

    require_can_mutate(actor.role)
    if not is_admin(actor.role):

        if role != USER or project_id != actor.project_id:
            raise ForbiddenError("Owners and team leads can only add plain users to their project.")
    if db.scalar(select(Assignee).where(Assignee.email == email)):
        raise ConflictError("An account with this email already exists.")
    if project_id is not None and db.get(Project, project_id) is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")
    account = Assignee(
        name=name,
        email=email,
        password_hash=hash_password(password),
        position=position,
        project_id=project_id,
        role=role,
        status=ACTIVE,
        approved_by=actor.id,

        notification_service.notify_member_added(
            db,
            member=account,
            actor=actor,
            project_name=project.name if project else "",
        )
        db.commit()
    return account

-- projects
CREATE TABLE projects (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active',
  owner_id INT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (owner_id) REFERENCES assignees(id)
);

CREATE TABLE assignees (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  position VARCHAR(127),
  project_id INT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

  FOREIGN KEY (project_id) REFERENCES projects(id)
);

  title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

  status VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'todo',

"""Analytics endpoints: project dashboard metrics."""
from fastapi import APIRouter, Query

from ...core.rules import is_admin
from ...core.errors import ForbiddenError, NotFoundError
from ...models import Project
from ...schemas.analytics import DashboardOut
from ..deps import CurrentUser, DbSession
from ...services import analytics_service

router = APIRouter(prefix="/analytics", tags=["analytics"])


@router.get("/dashboard", response_model=DashboardOut)
def project_dashboard(
    db: DbSession,
    user: CurrentUser,
    project_id: int = Query(..., ge=1),
) -> DashboardOut:
    """Dashboard metrics for one project.

    Access: admins across all projects; owners/users within their own project.
    """
    project = db.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")

    # Access scoping: admin across all projects; owner/user within own project.
    if not is_admin(user.role) and user.project_id != project_id:
        raise ForbiddenError("You can only view your own project dashboard.")

    return analytics_service.get_dashboard(db, project_id=project_id)

"""Project analytics dashboard computations."""
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from ..core.time import utc_now
from ..models import AnalyticsEvent, Assignee, Project, Task
from ..schemas.analytics import DashboardEventOut, DashboardOut


def record_event(
    db: Session,
    *,
    project_id: int,
    actor_id: int,
    event_type: str,
    task_id: int | None = None,
    payload: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Persist one analytics event for dashboard computations."""
    db.add(
        AnalyticsEvent(
            project_id=project_id,
            actor_id=actor_id,
            event_type=event_type,
            task_id=task_id,
            payload=payload,
        )
    )


def get_dashboard(db: Session, *, project_id: int) -> DashboardOut:
    """Compute dashboard metrics for one project."""
    project = db.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        from ..core.errors import NotFoundError

        raise NotFoundError("Project not found.")

    now = utc_now()
    # All tasks of the project.
    tasks = list(
        db.scalars(select(Task).where(Task.project_id == project_id)).all()
    )
    total = len(tasks)
    completed = [t for t in tasks if t.status == "completed"]
    pending = [t for t in tasks if t.status != "completed"]

    # Overdue: incomplete + due_date < today.
    today = now.date()
    overdue = [
        t
        for t in pending
        if t.due_date is not None and t.due_date < today
    ]

    completion_rate = round((len(completed) / total * 100), 1) if total else 0.0
    overdue_rate = round((len(overdue) / total * 100), 1) if total else 0.0

"""Notification endpoints: list, mark as read."""
from fastapi import APIRouter, Query

from ...models import Notification
from ...schemas import NotificationListOut, NotificationOut, MarkReadIn
from ..deps import CurrentUser, DbSession

router = APIRouter(prefix="/notifications", tags=["notifications"])


@router.get("", response_model=NotificationListOut)
def list_notifications(
    db: DbSession,
    user: CurrentUser,
    limit: int = Query(default=20, ge=1, le=100),
    offset: int = Query(default=0, ge=0),
    unread_only: bool = Query(default=False),
) -> NotificationListOut:
    query = db.query(Notification).where(Notification.user_id == user.id)
    if unread_only:
        query = query.where(Notification.read_at.is_(None))
    query = query.order_by(Notification.created_at.desc(), Notification.id.desc())
    total = query.count()
    items = query.limit(limit).offset(offset).all()
    unread = (
        db.query(Notification)
        .where(Notification.user_id == user.id, Notification.read_at.is_(None))
        .count()
    )
    return NotificationListOut(
        items=items, total=total, unread=unread, limit=limit, offset=offset
    )


@router.patch("/read", response_model=dict)
def mark_as_read(
    body: MarkReadIn,
    db: DbSession,
    user: CurrentUser,
) -> dict:
    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    for nid in body.notification_ids:
        n = db.get(Notification, nid)
        if n is not None and n.user_id == user.id and n.read_at is None:
            n.read_at = now
    db.commit()
    return {"marked": len(body.notification_ids)}

The workflow for every meaningful change. AGENTS.md holds the binding rules; this skill holds the procedure.

# Access Control

Source of truth: PROJECT_BRIEF.md (┬º5 rules, Accounts and Roles) and docs/ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md ┬º8. Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/2026-10-11-local-auth-and-roles.md`.

## Roles

Three cumulative roles: an admin can do everything a project owner and a user can do; a project owner everything a user can do.

- **Admin** ÔÇö owns the system: creates projects, assigns project owners, creates users anywhere, manages roles, confirms any join request, and sees every tab and all data.
- **Project owner** ÔÇö owns their projects: confirms or rejects join requests, sees all members and their statuses (pending/active), manages tasks and assignments, creates users inside their own projects. No project creation, no role changes.
- **User** ÔÇö works their tasks: views and completes assigned tasks, manages tasks in their own project. Must sign up and be confirmed before first login.

## Capability matrix

| Capability | User | Project Owner | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Log in (active accounts only) | Ô£ô | Ô£ô | Ô£ô |
| View and complete assigned tasks | own project | own projects | all projects |
| Create, edit, delete tasks | own project | own projects | all projects |
| Assign tasks to the project or a person | ÔÇö | own projects | all projects |
| Confirm or reject join requests | ÔÇö | own projects | all projects |
| Create users (role user) | ÔÇö | own projects | anywhere |
| Create projects, assign owners, manage roles | ÔÇö | ÔÇö | Ô£ô |

## Workflows

**New user (self-registration).** Open app ÔåÆ sign-up page (name, email, password, choose project) ÔåÆ account created as pending ÔåÆ relevant project owner confirms ÔåÆ user logs in ÔåÆ sees today's tasks. Pending users cannot log in.

**Project owner (enrollment).** Log in ÔåÆ Members tab ÔåÆ pending-requests section lists everyone waiting for their projects ÔåÆ confirm or reject ÔåÆ member becomes active and can log in. Roster shows every member with pending/active status.

**Admin (setup).** Log in ÔåÆ Projects tab ÔåÆ create project ÔåÆ assign its owner ÔåÆ optionally create users directly (active immediately). Can open every tab across all projects.

## Tabs per role (approved 2026-10-18)

- **Projects** ÔÇö admin only: create projects, list all, assign owners.
- **Members** ÔÇö all roles, scoped: user sees their own project's roster; owner sees their projects' rosters with pending/active statuses plus the pending-requests section; admin sees everyone including roles.
- **Tasks** ÔÇö all roles, scoped: user sees own project's tasks; owner their projects'; admin all.
- **Mine** ÔÇö owner and user (not admin, who can never be an assignee): tasks assigned to the logged-in person only (`assignee_id` = viewer), enforced by `TaskService.watchTasksAssignedTo`.
- **Approvals** live inside the Members tab as the pending-requests section (owner/admin only), not as a separate tab ÔÇö the brief asks for minimal screens.

Tab changes are business-rule changes; record them under `docs/decisions/`.

## Data scoping

Everyone sees only their own projects' data ÔÇö tasks, members, and requests are always filtered to the viewer's project(s). Only admins bypass the filter. Scoping is enforced in the application layer, not just by hiding tabs.

## Membership lifecycle

- Admins and project owners create active users directly.
- Self-registered users start as pending and cannot log in until the relevant project owner (or an admin) confirms them; confirmation records the owner's id in `approved_by`.
- Credentials live only in the local person table; passwords are salted hashes, never plain text.
- Key events raise an email notification through the device's mail app (proposed): a new sign-up notifies the project owner, approval or rejection notifies the user, a new assignment notifies the assignee.

## Enforcement

- Role, scope, and membership checks belong in the application/business-logic layer. The UI may hide actions, but must never be the only check.
- Changing roles, the matrix, workflows, tabs, or the approval flow is a business-rule change: propose and wait for approval (see `interactive-development`).

"""Subtasks: CRUD, ordering, project scoping, and viewer read-only rule."""
from helpers import auth_headers, bootstrap, list_items, sign_up

    """Admin, Bob in Alpha, and a task in Alpha."""

    task = client.post(
        "/api/v1/tasks",
        json={"project_id": project["id"], "title": "Release"},
        headers=headers,
    ).json()
    return headers, project, bob, task, auth_headers(client, "bob@example.com")


def _add_subtask(client, headers, task_id, title, sort_order=0):
    response = client.post(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/subtasks",
        json={"task_id": task_id, "title": title, "sort_order": sort_order},
        headers=headers,
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    return response.json()


def test_subtask_crud_round_trip_keeps_sort_order(client):
    headers, _, _, task, bob_headers = _setup(client)
    late = _add_subtask(client, bob_headers, task["id"], "Write docs", 2)
    early = _add_subtask(client, bob_headers, task["id"], "Write tests", 1)

    listed = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/{task['id']}/subtasks", headers=bob_headers
    )
    assert listed.status_code == 200
    body = listed.json()
    assert body["total"] == 2
    assert [row["title"] for row in list_items(body)] == [
        "Write tests",
        "Write docs",
    ]

    updated = client.patch(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/subtasks/{late['id']}",
        json={"title": "Write the docs", "completed": True, "sort_order": 0},
        headers=bob_headers,
    )
    assert updated.status_code == 200, updated.text
    assert updated.json()["title"] == "Write the docs"
    assert updated.json()["completed"] is True
    assert updated.json()["sort_order"] == 0

    reordered = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/{task['id']}/subtasks", headers=bob_headers
    ).json()
    assert [row["title"] for row in list_items(reordered)] == [
        "Write the docs",
        "Write tests",
    ]

    deleted = client.delete(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/subtasks/{early['id']}", headers=bob_headers
    )
    assert deleted.status_code == 200
    remaining = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/{task['id']}/subtasks", headers=headers
    ).json()
    assert remaining["total"] == 1
    assert list_items(remaining)[0]["id"] == late["id"]

    _, admin_headers, project_a = bootstrap(client, "Alpha")

"""Bulk task actions: partial success, validation, notifications, viewers."""
from helpers import auth_headers, bootstrap, sign_up


def _setup(client, count=3):

    _, headers, project = bootstrap(client, "Alpha")
    bob = sign_up(client, "bob@example.com", name="Bob", project_id=project["id"])
    client.post(f"/api/v1/members/{bob['id']}/confirm", headers=headers)
    tasks = []
    for i in range(count):
        tasks.append(
            client.post(
                "/api/v1/tasks",
                json={"project_id": project["id"], "title": f"Task {i + 1}"},
                headers=headers,
            ).json()
        )
    return headers, project, bob, tasks, auth_headers(client, "bob@example.com")


def test_bulk_complete_reports_each_task_outcome(client):
    headers, _, _, tasks, _ = _setup(client)
    ids = [t["id"] for t in tasks[:2]] + [9999]

    response = client.post(
        "/api/v1/tasks/bulk/complete", json={"task_ids": ids}, headers=headers
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    body = response.json()
    assert body["total"] == 3
    assert body["succeeded"] == 2
    assert body["failed"] == 1
    failures = [row for row in body["results"] if not row["success"]]
    assert failures[0]["task_id"] == 9999
    assert failures[0]["error"] == "Task not found."

    listed = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/tasks?project_id={tasks[0]['project_id']}", headers=headers
    ).json()["items"]
    statuses = {row["title"]: row["status"] for row in listed}
    assert statuses["Task 1"] == "completed"
    assert statuses["Task 2"] == "completed"
    assert statuses["Task 3"] == "todo"


def test_bulk_reassign_validates_assignee_and_notifies(client):

    assigned = client.post(
        "/api/v1/tasks/bulk/reassign",

            "name": name,
            "email": email,
            "password": "password123",
            "project_id": project_id,
            "role": role,
        },
        headers=headers,
    )
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    return response.json()

    project_b = client.post(
        "/api/v1/projects", json={"name": "Beta"}, headers=admin_headers
    ).json()
    _account(
        client, admin_headers, "Tara Lead", "tara@example.com",
        project_a["id"], "team_lead",
    )

    created = client.post(
        "/api/v1/members",
        json={
            "name": "New User",

"""Analytics dashboard and project archive/restore."""
from datetime import date, timedelta

from helpers import auth_headers, bootstrap, list_items, sign_up


def test_dashboard_counts_tasks_and_lists_events(client):
    _, headers, project = bootstrap(client, "Alpha")
    yesterday = (date.today() - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
    next_week = (date.today() + timedelta(days=7)).isoformat()

    overdue = client.post(
        "/api/v1/tasks",
        json={
            "project_id": project["id"],
            "title": "Overdue",
            "priority": "low",
            "due_date": yesterday,
        },
        headers=headers,
    ).json()
    client.post(
        "/api/v1/tasks",
        json={
            "project_id": project["id"],
            "title": "Upcoming",
            "priority": "high",
            "due_date": next_week,
        },
        headers=headers,
    )
    done = client.post(
        "/api/v1/tasks",
        json={"project_id": project["id"], "title": "Done", "priority": "medium"},
        headers=headers,
    ).json()
    client.patch(f"/api/v1/tasks/{done['id']}/complete", headers=headers)

    # A subtask event must not break dashboard serialization.
    client.post(
        f"/api/v1/tasks/{overdue['id']}/subtasks",
        json={"task_id": overdue["id"], "title": "Checklist"},
        headers=headers,
    )

    response = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/analytics/dashboard?project_id={project['id']}", headers=headers
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    body = response.json()
    assert body["project_id"] == project["id"]
    assert body["project_name"] == "Alpha"
    assert body["total_tasks"] == 3
    assert body["completed_tasks"] == 1
    assert body["pending_tasks"] == 2
    assert body["overdue_tasks"] == 1
    assert body["completion_rate"] == 33.3
    assert body["overdue_rate"] == 33.3
    assert body["priority_mix"] == {"low": 1, "medium": 1, "high": 1}
    assert body["velocity_per_week"] == 0.2

    events = body["recent_events"]
    assert [e["event_type"] for e in events] == [
        "subtask_created",
        "task_completed",
        "task_created",
        "task_created",
        "task_created",
    ]
    assert {e["actor_name"] for e in events} == {"Root Admin"}
    assert events[0]["task_id"] == overdue["id"]


def test_dashboard_is_scoped_and_validated(client):
    _, headers, project_a = bootstrap(client, "Alpha")
    beta = client.post(
        "/api/v1/projects", json={"name": "Beta"}, headers=headers
    ).json()
    bob = sign_up(client, "bob@example.com", name="Bob",
                  project_id=project_a["id"])
    client.post(f"/api/v1/members/{bob['id']}/confirm", headers=headers)
    bob_headers = auth_headers(client, "bob@example.com")

    denied = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/analytics/dashboard?project_id={beta['id']}",
        headers=bob_headers,
    )
    assert denied.status_code == 403
    assert denied.json()["detail"] == (
        "You can only view your own project dashboard."
    )

    own = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/analytics/dashboard?project_id={project_a['id']}",
        headers=bob_headers,
    )
    assert own.status_code == 200

    admin_any = client.get(
        f"/api/v1/analytics/dashboard?project_id={beta['id']}", headers=headers
    )
    assert admin_any.status_code == 200

    missing = client.get(
        "/api/v1/analytics/dashboard?project_id=9999", headers=headers
    )
    assert missing.status_code == 404
    assert missing.json()["detail"] == "Project not found."

    unvalidated = client.get("/api/v1/analytics/dashboard", headers=headers)
    assert unvalidated.status_code == 422


def test_archive_hides_a_project_and_restore_brings_it_back(client):
    _, headers, project = bootstrap(client, "Alpha")
    bob = sign_up(client, "bob@example.com", name="Bob",
                  project_id=project["id"])
    client.post(f"/api/v1/members/{bob['id']}/confirm", headers=headers)
    bob_headers = auth_headers(client, "bob@example.com")

    archived = client.patch(
        f"/api/v1/projects/{project['id']}/archive", headers=headers
    )
    assert archived.status_code == 200
    assert archived.json()["status"] == "archived"

    default_list = client.get("/api/v1/projects").json()
    assert default_list["total"] == 0
    assert list_items(default_list) == []

    with_archived = client.get("/api/v1/projects?include_archived=true").json()
    assert [p["name"] for p in list_items(with_archived)] == ["Alpha"]
    assert list_items(with_archived)[0]["status"] == "archived"

    denied = client.patch(
        f"/api/v1/projects/{project['id']}/restore", headers=bob_headers
    )
    assert denied.status_code == 403
    assert denied.json()["detail"] == "Only an admin can do this."

    restored = client.patch(
        f"/api/v1/projects/{project['id']}/restore", headers=headers
    )
    assert restored.status_code == 200
    assert restored.json()["status"] == "active"

    back = client.get("/api/v1/projects").json()
    assert [p["name"] for p in list_items(back)] == ["Alpha"]

1: # Automatic Logout on an Authenticated 401
2: 
3: - Date: 2026-10-25
4: - Status: approved by the user on 2026-10-25 and implemented (automatic logout
5:   with a message)
6: - Context: E2E E8 and gap G2. When the API rejected an authenticated request
7:   with 401, the UI stayed on `/home` with `Invalid or expired token` and a Retry
8:   button. A genuinely expired token could never recover, so the user was stuck
9:   until a manual logout ÔÇö with no indication that the session was over.
10: - Options considered:
11:   1. **End the session and return to login with a notice (chosen)** ÔÇö matches
12:      the meaning of 401, keeps the user in control, no API change.
13:   2. Keep the error screen with Retry ÔÇö rejected: no request can succeed with an
14:      invalid token, so Retry is a dead end.
15:   3. Silent logout without a message ÔÇö rejected: the sudden return to login
16:      looks like data loss or a bug.
17:   4. Refresh-token flow ÔÇö rejected for now: the API issues no refresh token and
18:      adding one changes the contract.
19: - Decision:
20:   - `ApiClient` exposes `setUnauthorizedHandler`; `HttpApiClient` remembers
21:     whether a token was attached to the request and invokes the handler on 401;
22:   - 401 responses without a token (login, sign-up) never invoke it, so a wrong
23:     password keeps its normal `Wrong email or password.` message;
24:   - the handler clears the token, closes the session, shows
25:     `Your session expired. Log in again.` on the login screen and lets the
26:     router redirect;
27:   - state changes are deferred to a microtask because the callback runs while a
28:     provider is building and Riverpod forbids modifying another provider during
29:     initialization;
30:   - the notice is cleared on the next login attempt and on a normal logout.
31: - Implementation:
32:   - `task_planner/lib/services/api_client.dart` ÔÇö handler and token-aware 401;
33:   - `task_planner/lib/app/app.dart` ÔÇö wiring, token/session cleanup, microtask;

# Team Lead and Viewer Roles

- Date: 2026-10-27
- Status: approved as part of the 2026-10-27 "all features including AI" scope;
  implemented
- Context: the backend rules already defined `TEAM_LEAD` and `VIEWER`, and the
  member messages mentioned team leads, but `Role` in
  `backend/app/schemas/account.py` only accepted `admin`, `project_owner`, and
  `user`. The API therefore rejected both roles with 422, and the Flutter UI had
  no way to assign them. Viewer read-only enforcement also had a hole: subtask
  mutations never called `require_can_mutate`.
- Options considered:
  1. **Keep three roles and remove the dead constants (chosen against)** ÔÇö
     simplest, but drops the delegation and read-only capabilities the product
     catalogue already promises.
  2. **Officialise both roles in the schema and enforce them server-side
     (chosen)** ÔÇö matches the planned capability matrix, no new tables, no new
     dependencies.
  3. Client-only role checks ÔÇö rejected: the server is the enforcer and the UI
     check is only a convenience.
- Decision:
  - cumulative order: `admin` > `project_owner` > `team_lead` > `user` >
    `viewer`;
  - `team_lead` may add plain users and confirm pending members **in its own
    project only**; it cannot add elevated roles, change roles, create projects,
    or assign owners;
  - `viewer` is read-only: it may list projects, members, tasks, subtasks, and
    dashboards, but every mutation returns 403 `Viewers cannot make changes.`;
  - `admin` remains the only role that creates projects, assigns owners, and
    changes roles.
- Implementation:
  - `backend/app/schemas/account.py` ÔÇö `Role` Literal extended;
  - `backend/app/services/subtask.py` ÔÇö `require_can_mutate` on create, update,
    and delete;
  - `backend/app/services/members.py` ÔÇö team-lead branch already present, now
    reachable;
  - `backend/app/core/rules.py` ÔÇö role constants and helpers (unchanged
    contract, now enforced end-to-end);
  - `backend/tests/test_roles.py`, `backend/tests/test_subtasks.py` ÔÇö role
    matrix, delegation limits, viewer read-only on tasks, subtasks, members,
    projects, and archive.
- Verification:
  - backend pytest **81/81** (`docker compose exec -T api python -m pytest
    tests -q`), including 22 new tests for notifications, subtasks, bulk
    actions, roles, analytics, and archive;
  - Flutter **75/75** and `flutter analyze` 0 errors / 0 warnings (17 infos).
- Reverses: none. Extends the 2026-10-11 local-auth-and-roles decision.
- Still open: none for v1; AI-specific permissions will be decided with the AI
  milestone.

# Mark-Read Notification Contract

- Date: 2026-10-27
- Status: approved as part of the 2026-10-27 "all features including AI" scope;
  implemented
- Context: `PATCH /api/v1/notifications/read` returned the number of IDs sent by
  the client, not the number actually marked. It silently skipped notifications
  that belonged to another account. A client could therefore believe it had
  marked a foreign notification as read. This was defect BD8 in the Phase 0
  audit.
- Options considered:
  1. **Reject foreign or unknown IDs with 403/404 (chosen against)** ÔÇö reveals
     whether another account's notification exists and makes partial batches
     awkward for a mobile client that may retry.
  2. **Ignore foreign/unknown IDs but report the real count (chosen)** ÔÇö keeps
     the endpoint idempotent and batch-friendly, gives the client truthful
     feedback.
  3. Return the requested count (previous behavior) ÔÇö rejected: misleading.
- Decision:
  - only notifications owned by the caller and still unread are marked;
  - unknown or foreign IDs are ignored silently;
  - the response is `{"marked": <actually marked>}`, so replaying the same
    request returns `0`.
- Implementation:
  - `backend/app/api/routers/notifications.py` ÔÇö count incremented only inside
    the ownership/unread check;
  - `backend/tests/test_notifications.py` ÔÇö foreign ID returns 0, owner marks 1,
    replay returns 0, `unread_only` and the `unread` counter agree.
- Verification: backend pytest **81/81**; no Flutter API change needed (the
  service already ignored the value).
- Reverses: none.

# Phase 0 Stabilization Decisions

- Date: 2026-10-27
- Status: approved as part of the 2026-10-27 "all features including AI" scope;
  implemented
- Context: the 2026-10-27 audit of `.kilo/plans/proposal-progress.md` found P0/P1
  defects that made the product unsafe to extend: a cold start lost the session,
  pagination invalidated providers instead of loading more rows, the subtask
  client called routes the API does not expose, a subtask analytics event broke
  dashboard serialization, and SMTP ran inside the request path. This record
  covers the cross-cutting decisions; role and notification contracts have
  their own records.
- Decisions:
  1. **Session restore before routing.** `TaskPlannerApp` reads the persisted
     JWT, validates it with `/auth/me`, hydrates `sessionUserIdProvider`, and
     only then sets `sessionReadyProvider`. The router keeps the splash screen
     until the flag is set, so a cold start never flashes the login page. A
     rejected token is deleted from storage and the app lands on login.
  2. **Real page accumulation.** `PaginatedNotifier` loads page one on build,
     appends pages on scroll, deduplicates by row identity, stops when the
     server total is reached, ignores stale/shared concurrent responses with a
     generation counter, and reloads page one quietly after a mutation
     (`DataSync` tick). Screens call `notifier.loadMore()` / `refresh()`;
     `ref.invalidate` is no longer used for scrolling.
  3. **One subtask route shape.** `GET/POST /tasks/{task_id}/subtasks` for the
     collection and `PATCH/DELETE /tasks/subtasks/{subtask_id}` for one row.
     The Flutter `SubtaskService` was calling `/subtasks/{id}` and now matches
     the documented contract.
  4. **Analytics event vocabulary includes `subtask_created`.** The dashboard
     response validates event types, so recording a subtask without adding the
     type made `GET /analytics/dashboard` fail with a 500 once a checklist item
     existed.
  5. **SMTP never blocks a request.** `email_service.send_async` submits to a
     two-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor`; `notification_service` uses it. Without
     SMTP configuration the call is a no-op.
- Implementation:
  - `task_planner/lib/app/app.dart`, `task_planner/lib/app/router.dart`,
    `task_planner/lib/providers/session_providers.dart`,
    `task_planner/lib/main.dart` ÔÇö session restore;
  - `task_planner/lib/providers/data_providers.dart` ÔÇö `PaginatedNotifier`,
    `dataSyncTickProvider`, paginated providers;
  - `task_planner/lib/screens/{projects,members,tasks,my_tasks,planner}_tab.dart`,
    `task_planner/lib/widgets/tasks/task_list.dart` ÔÇö load more / refresh;
  - `task_planner/lib/services/{project,member,task}_service.dart` ÔÇö page

  - `task_planner/lib/services/subtask_service.dart` ÔÇö corrected paths;

  - `backend/app/schemas/analytics.py` ÔÇö event type;

    `backend/app/services/notification_service.py` ÔÇö async email.

1: # Task Planner
2: 
3: Flutter mobile client with a FastAPI + MySQL backend and a browser-based
4: phpMyAdmin instance for local development.
5: 
6: The app is online-only: it talks to the API and stores no task data locally.
7: The API owns authentication, roles, membership approval, and task rules.
8: 
9: ## Repository layout
10: 
11: | Path | Purpose |
12: |---|---|
13: | `task_planner/` | Flutter app (Riverpod, go_router, HTTP). |
14: | `backend/` | FastAPI API, SQLAlchemy models, Alembic migrations, pytest suite. |
15: | `compose.yaml` | Local MySQL + API + phpMyAdmin stack. |
16: | `docs/` | Architecture, implementation plan, and decision records. |
17: 
18: ## Quick start
19: 
20: On a fresh clone, after installing the prerequisites below:
21: 
22: ```powershell
23: Copy-Item .env.example .env
24: # edit .env and replace the placeholders
25: docker compose up --build -d
26: docker compose ps
27: ```
28: 
29: In a second terminal:
30: 
31: ```powershell
32: cd task_planner
33: flutter pub get
34: flutter run
35: ```
36: 
37: The API is at <http://127.0.0.1:8000>, Swagger at
38: <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs>, and phpMyAdmin at <http://127.0.0.1:8080>.
39: The sections below explain each step and the Android/device variants.
40: 
41: ## 1. Prerequisites
42: 
43: - Git.
44: - Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS) or Docker Engine with Compose v2.
45: - Flutter 3.47+ and Dart 3.13+.
46: - Android Studio, Android SDK, and an emulator for Android development.
47: - Optional: VS Code. Open the repository folder and accept the recommended
48:   Flutter, Dart, Python, and Docker extensions.
49: - Python 3.11+ only if you run the backend directly on the host instead of
50:   in Docker.
51: 
52: Flutter stays on the host rather than in a Dev Container so emulator, USB
53: device, and desktop debugging work normally. Only the API, MySQL, and
54: phpMyAdmin run in Docker.
55: 
56: Verify the tools from a new terminal:
57: 
58: ```powershell
59: docker --version
60: docker compose version
61: flutter doctor
62: ```
63: 
64: For Android, accept the SDK licenses and check for an emulator:
65: 
66: ```powershell
67: flutter doctor --android-licenses
68: flutter emulators
69: adb devices
70: ```
71: 
72: If `docker` is not found on Windows, make sure Docker Desktop is running and
73: open a new terminal. A per-user install may need Docker Desktop's
74: `resources\bin` directory on `PATH`.
75: 
76: ## 2. Clone the repository
77: 
78: ```powershell
79: git clone https://github.com/chocksma3iil/Task_planner_mobile_app.git
80: cd Task_planner_mobile_app
81: ```
82: 
83: Use your fork instead of the upstream URL if you have one.
84: 
85: ## 3. Configure environment variables
86: 
87: The Docker stack reads the root `.env`. It is Git-ignored. Skip this copy if
88: `.env` already exists.
89: 
90: ```powershell
91: Copy-Item .env.example .env
92: ```
93: 
94: Edit `.env` and replace the placeholder passwords and `SECRET_KEY`. Use
95: URL-safe characters in `MYSQL_PASSWORD` because it becomes part of the
96: database URL. The defaults for ports are:
97: 
98: - API: `8000`
99: - phpMyAdmin: `8080`
100: - MySQL: `3306` inside the Docker network only
101: 
102: The API and phpMyAdmin bind to `127.0.0.1` by default. MySQL has no host port,
103: so the stack does not conflict with a MySQL installation on your machine and
104: does not expose the database to the LAN.
105: 
106: `backend/.env` is only for running FastAPI directly on the host. It is not
107: needed for the Compose flow. Never commit either `.env` file or use development
108: credentials for shared or production systems.
109: 
110: ## 4. Start Docker services
111: 
112: From the repository root:
113: 
114: ```powershell
115: docker compose up --build -d
116: docker compose ps
117: ```
118: 
119: Wait until `mysql` and `api` are healthy. First start pulls images and
120: initializes the database, so it can take a few minutes.
121: 
122: Useful commands:
123: 
124: ```powershell
125: docker compose logs -f api
126: docker compose logs -f mysql
127: docker compose down
128: ```
129: 
130: `docker compose down` keeps the named database volume. Do **not** use
131: `docker compose down -v` unless you intend to delete all local Docker database
132: data.
133: 
134: ## 5. Initialize the database
135: 
136: The API container runs this before Uvicorn starts:
137: 
138: ```text
139: alembic upgrade head
140: ```
141: 
142: On a fresh volume this applies `backend/alembic/versions/0001_initial.py` and
143: creates `projects`, `assignees`, `tasks`, and `alembic_version`. The MySQL init
144: script also creates `task_planner_test` and grants the app user access, so the
145: pytest suite works without manual database setup.
146:

151: ```

153: The final `task_planner` argument selects the database; without it, MySQL
154: returns `ERROR 1046 (3D000): No database selected`. Use the `MYSQL_PASSWORD`
155: value from `.env` when prompted. You can also inspect
156: `alembic_version` there. The Compose database is separate from any MySQL
157: installation already running on the host; it does not overwrite or reset it.
158:

161: matches, `alembic stamp 0001_initial` can mark it as current. Never do this
162: against a shared database without authorization.
163: 
164: ## 6. Run the Flutter application
165: 
166: From the repository root, in a second terminal:
167: 
168: ```powershell
169: cd task_planner
170: flutter pub get
171: flutter run
172: ```
173: 
174: The app uses `http://localhost:8000/api/v1` by default, which works for Windows
175: desktop, web, and the iOS simulator. For other targets, pass the full base URL,
176: including `/api/v1`.
177: 
178: | Target | Command |
179: |---|---|
180: | Windows desktop | `flutter run -d windows` |
181: | Android emulator | `flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8000/api/v1` |
182: | Android physical device over USB | `adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000` then `flutter run --dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/v1` |
183: | Physical device over LAN | Set `API_BIND=0.0.0.0` in `.env`, run `docker compose up -d api`, then use `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL=http://YOUR_LAN_IP:8000/api/v1` |
184: 
185: LAN binding exposes the API on your network. Use it only on a trusted network
186: and allow port `8000` through the host firewall if needed. The development API
187: uses HTTP; release builds should use HTTPS. Android debug builds allow local
188: HTTP. iOS blocks cleartext HTTP by default, so iOS device development needs
189: HTTPS or a reviewed ATS exception.
190: 
191: The first account registered on a fresh database becomes the admin. Later
192: sign-ups join a project as pending members until the project owner or an admin
193: confirms them. Passwords must be at least 8 characters.
194: 
195: ## 7. Access phpMyAdmin
196: 
197: Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080>. The login page is already configured for the
198: local `mysql` container. These are the MySQL credentials, not the app account
199: you create in Flutter.
200: 
201: - Username: `task_planner`
202: - Password: `MYSQL_PASSWORD` from the root `.env`
203: 
204: phpMyAdmin is bound to loopback only. Do not expose it publicly.
205: 
206: ## 8. Run tests and checks
207: 
208: Backend tests run inside the API container against `task_planner_test`:
209: 
210: ```powershell
211: docker compose exec api python -m pytest tests -q
212: ```
213: 
214: Flutter checks do not need the backend:
215: 
216: ```powershell
217: cd task_planner
218: flutter analyze
219: flutter test
220: ```
221: 
222: The Flutter widget tests use an in-memory fake API client. The backend test
223: suite truncates its test tables between tests, so `TEST_DATABASE_URL` must
224: always point at a disposable local database.
225: 
226: ## 9. Troubleshooting
227: 
228: | Symptom | Check |
229: |---|---|
230: | `docker: command not found` | Start Docker Desktop and open a new terminal; verify `PATH`. |
231: | `docker-credential-desktop` not found | Open a new terminal after installing Docker Desktop, or add its `resources\bin` directory to `PATH`. |
232: | Port `8000` or `8080` already in use | Stop the local service or change `API_PORT` / `PHPMYADMIN_PORT` in `.env`, then restart Compose. |
233: | API container is unhealthy | Run `docker compose logs api`; confirm `mysql` is healthy and the API uses hostname `mysql`, not `localhost`. |
234: | phpMyAdmin cannot log in | Use user `task_planner` and the password from `.env`; leave the default server. Check `docker compose logs mysql`. |
235: | `ERROR 1046 (3D000): No database selected` | Add the database name to the MySQL command: `docker compose exec mysql mysql -utask_planner -p task_planner -e "SHOW TABLES;"`. |
236: | `Access denied` after changing MySQL passwords | MySQL applies `MYSQL_*` values only when the volume is first initialized. Use the original credentials or change the database user explicitly; do not delete the volume without a backup. |
237: | Alembic says a table already exists | The database was not created by Alembic. Use a fresh volume, or back up and stamp only after verifying the schema. |
238: | Android app cannot reach the API | Use `10.0.2.2` for the emulator, or `adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000` for USB. Debug builds allow local HTTP; release builds do not. |
239: | `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is missing | Use the Compose test command above, or create `backend/.env` for a host-run backend. |

242: 
243: This repository does not create or expose a shared database. If your team
244: provides one, the maintainer supplies the host, port, database name, username,
245: password, and phpMyAdmin URL separately. Do not put those credentials in the

# Team lead member management in the UI, and role refresh on app resume

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Status:** Implemented and verified
- **Scope:** Phase 0 validation follow-up (v1.0 access-control correctness)
- **Related:** `docs/decisions/2026-10-27-team-lead-and-viewer-roles.md`,
  `docs/decisions/2026-10-27-phase-0-stabilization.md`, `TEST_PLAN.md` ┬º17

## Context

The server has allowed `team_lead` accounts to add plain users and confirm
pending members of their own project since the extended roles were introduced.
The Flutter Members tab still treated only admins and project owners as
managers: a team lead saw no pending section, no status chips, no **Add user**
button and no **Confirm** button. The backend tests were green, so the feature
looked complete while the UI made it unreachable.

A second gap surfaced during E15: when an admin changed a signed-in account's
role, the app kept the old role until the user logged out or restarted. The
session token stayed valid, so a viewer could keep an old team-lead shell (the
server still returned 403 on every mutation, but the UI lied).

## Decisions

1. **Members tab capabilities follow the server rules.**
   - `canManage` is true for admins, project owners and team leads.
   - Team leads see the pending/active status chips and the **Add user**
     button for their own project.
   - `canConfirm` accepts an admin anywhere, or an owner/team lead whose
     project matches the member's project.
   - Role changes remain admin-only; team leads never see the role menu.
2. **The role is re-read when the app returns to the foreground.**
   `TaskPlannerApp` observes the app lifecycle and emits a `DataSync` ping on
   `AppLifecycleState.resumed`. `currentUserProvider` already re-fetches
   `/auth/me` on every ping, so the visible tabs and actions update without a
   logout. There is still no real-time push while the app stays in the
   foreground; a reload or a resume is the refresh boundary.

## Consequences

- Team leads can now complete the member workflow the API already allowed.
- A role change made elsewhere takes effect when the user returns to the app;
  a foreground app keeps its snapshot until the next refresh. This is
  acceptable for v1 and documented as residual gap R4 in `TEST_PLAN.md` ┬º17.6.
- No schema, endpoint, or dependency change.

## Verification

- Widget tests: `members_tab_test.dart` (team lead confirms a pending user,
  no role menu, Add user visible) and `home_screen_test.dart` (resumed app
  switches a user to viewer tabs) ÔÇö full suite **81/81**.
- Backend suite **81/81**; `flutter analyze` **0 errors / 0 warnings**.
- E2E **E15 PASS**: team lead confirms a pending Alpha user, escalation calls
  return 403, viewer gets 403 on 15 mutations, and the shell refreshes after
  reload (viewer, then user again).

The workflow for every meaningful change. AGENTS.md holds the binding rules; this skill holds the procedure.

**Step 1 ÔÇö Inspect.** Read AGENTS.md, PROJECT_BRIEF.md, and relevant docs. Inspect existing files, find reusable code and tests. Do not assume the repository is empty.

**Step 2 ÔÇö Understand.** Identify the intended user outcome, the relevant business rules, missing information, and conflicting requirements. State assumptions explicitly.

**Step 3 ÔÇö Propose.** Before changing files, describe the problem, the solution, the files that would change, new dependencies or architectural impact, and how it will be tested.

**Step 4 ÔÇö Stop and wait.** Request explicit approval. Do not implement until approval is received. Architectural changes need a new proposal even when discovered mid-implementation.

**Step 5 ÔÇö Implement minimally.** Make only the approved changes. Reuse existing utilities and patterns. No unrelated refactoring, no silent scope expansion.

**Step 6 ÔÇö Verify.** Run relevant tests and checks, inspect the changes, report actual results and unresolved failures. Never invent test results.

**Step 7 ÔÇö Record and stop.** Update relevant documentation, report what changed and what remains, then stop and wait.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from sqlalchemy import delete, func, select
...
def purge_old_events(db: Session, *, days: int) -> int:
    """Delete analytics events older than [days] and return the row count.

    Dashboard KPIs do not depend on the raw log (velocity uses task
    completion timestamps), so pruning old events only shortens the
    "recent activity" history.
    """
    if days <= 0:
        raise ValueError("days must be positive.")
    cutoff = utc_now() - timedelta(days=days)
    result = db.execute(
        delete(AnalyticsEvent).where(AnalyticsEvent.created_at < cutoff)
    )
    db.commit()
    return int(result.rowcount or 0)
```

import argparse

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m app.maintenance")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    purge = sub.add_parser("purge-events", help="Delete analytics events past retention.")
    purge.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DAYS)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        deleted = purge_old_events(db, days=args.days)
    print(f"Deleted {deleted} analytics event(s) older than {args.days} days.")
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":

def purge_old_events(db: Session, *, days: int) -> int:
    """Delete analytics events older than [days] and return the row count.

    Dashboard KPIs do not depend on the raw log (velocity is computed from
    task completion timestamps), so pruning only shortens the "recent
    activity" history.
    """
    if days <= 0:
        raise ValueError("days must be a positive number of days.")
    cutoff = utc_now() - timedelta(days=days)
    result = db.execute(
        delete(AnalyticsEvent).where(AnalyticsEvent.created_at < cutoff)
    )
    db.commit()
    return int(result.rowcount or 0)

"""In-process login throttle.

The first release runs a single API process, so a small in-memory sliding
window is enough to blunt password guessing without a new dependency or a
shared store. Replace it with a shared store before running several workers.
"""
from collections import defaultdict, deque
from threading import Lock
from time import monotonic

from .config import LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS, LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS
from .errors import RateLimitedError


class LoginThrottle:
    """Counts failed logins per key inside a sliding window."""

    def __init__(self, *, max_attempts: int, window_seconds: float) -> None:
        self.max_attempts = max_attempts
        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
        self._failures: dict[str, deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)
        self._lock = Lock()

    def check(self, key: str, *, now: float | None = None) -> None:
        """Raise RateLimitedError when [key] used all its attempts."""
        moment = monotonic() if now is None else now
        with self._lock:
            attempts = self._recent(key, moment)
            if len(attempts) >= self.max_attempts:
                raise RateLimitedError()

    def fail(self, key: str, *, now: float | None = None) -> None:
        """Record one failed attempt for [key]."""
        moment = monotonic() if now is None else now
        with self._lock:
            attempts = self._recent(key, moment)
            attempts.append(moment)

    def reset(self, key: str) -> None:
        """Forget the failures of [key] after a successful login."""
        with self._lock:
            self._failures.pop(key, None)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Forget every counter (tests and maintenance)."""
        with self._lock:
            self._failures.clear()

    def _recent(self, key: str, moment: float) -> deque[float]:
        attempts = self._failures[key]
        cutoff = moment - self.window_seconds
        while attempts and attempts[0] <= cutoff:
            attempts.popleft()
        if not attempts:
            self._failures.pop(key, None)  # careful: we return attempts afterwards
        return attempts
```

The first release runs a single API process, so a small in-memory sliding
window blunts password guessing without a new dependency or a shared store.
Replace it with a shared store before running several API workers.

from collections import defaultdict, deque
from threading import Lock
from time import monotonic

from .config import LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS, LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS
from .errors import RateLimitedError


class LoginThrottle:
    """Counts failed logins per key inside a sliding window."""

    def __init__(self, *, max_attempts: int, window_seconds: float) -> None:
        self.max_attempts = max_attempts
        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
        self._failures: dict[str, deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)
        self._lock = Lock()

    def check(self, key: str, *, now: float | None = None) -> None:
        """Raise [RateLimitedError] when [key] used all its attempts."""
        moment = monotonic() if now is None else now
        with self._lock:
            if len(self._recent(key, moment)) >= self.max_attempts:
                raise RateLimitedError()

    def fail(self, key: str, *, now: float | None = None) -> None:
        """Record one failed attempt for [key]."""

            self._recent(key, moment).append(moment)

        with self._lock:
            self._failures.clear()

    def _recent(self, key: str, moment: float) -> deque[float]:
        """Drop attempts older than the window and return the rest."""
        attempts = self._failures[key]
        cutoff = moment - self.window_seconds
        while attempts and attempts[0] <= cutoff:
            attempts.popleft()
        return attempts

"""NF5 perf smoke: 3 projects / 50 members / 200 tasks.

Runs against the temporary API on 127.0.0.1:8001, backed by the test
database. Prints a JSON report with the timings collected.
"""
import json
import statistics
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1"
PASSWORD = "Passw0rd!23"
ADMIN_EMAIL = "perf-admin@example.com"


def request(method, path, body=None, token=None):
    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, method=method)
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if token:
        req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as response:
            raw = response.read()
            return response.status, json.loads(raw) if raw else None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{method} {path} -> {error.code}: {error.read()[:500]}")


def timed(method, path, token, samples=5):
    """One warm-up call, then [samples] measured calls in milliseconds."""
    request(method, path, token=token)
    durations = []
    for _ in range(samples):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        request(method, path, token=token)
        durations.append(round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2))
    return {
        "samples_ms": durations,
        "median_ms": round(statistics.median(durations), 2),
        "max_ms": max(durations),
    }


status, admin = request(
    "POST",
    "/auth/signup",
    {
        "name": "Perf Admin",
        "email": ADMIN_EMAIL,
        "password": PASSWORD,
    },
)
assert status == 201, status
assert admin["role"] == "admin", f"Expected a fresh database, got {admin['role']}"
_, login = request("POST", "/auth/login", {"email": ADMIN_EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD})
token = login["access_token"]

projects = []
for name in ("Perf Alpha", "Perf Beta", "Perf Gamma"):
    status, project = request(
        "POST", "/projects", {"name": name, "description": "NF5 smoke"}, token
    )
    assert status == 201, status
    projects.append(project)

# 50 members split 17 / 17 / 16.
members = []
for index in range(50):
    project = projects[index % 3]
    status, member = request(
        "POST",
        "/members",
        {
            "name": f"Perf Member {index + 1:02d}",
            "email": f"perf.member{index + 1:02d}@example.com",
            "password": PASSWORD,
            "position": "Tester" if index % 2 else "Analyst",
            "project_id": project["id"],
            "role": "user",
        },
        token,
    )
    assert status == 201, status
    members.append(member)

# 200 tasks spread over the projects; every 5th completed, a mix of dates.
priorities = ["low", "medium", "high"]
today = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
dates = [None, today, "2026-11-15", "2020-01-01"]
checklist = []
for index in range(200):
    project = projects[index % 3]
    candidates = [m for m in members if m["project_id"] == project["id"]]
    assignee = None if index % 4 == 0 else candidates[index % len(candidates)]
    status, task = request(
        "POST",
        "/tasks",
        {
            "project_id": project["id"],
            "title": f"Perf task {index + 1:03d}",
            "description": "NF5 smoke task",
            "priority": priorities[index % 3],
            "due_date": dates[index % 4],
            "assignee_id": assignee["id"] if assignee else None,
        },
        token,
    )
    assert status == 201, status
    if index % 5 == 0:
        request("PATCH", f"/tasks/{task['id']}/complete", token=token)
    checklist.append(task["id"])

alpha = projects[0]["id"]
# Page through the whole project list the way the app does (20 per page).
page_offsets = list(range(0, 100, 20))
paging = []
for offset in page_offsets:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    status, page = request(
        "GET", f"/tasks?project_id={alpha}&limit=20&offset={offset}", token=token
    )
    elapsed = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
    paging.append({"offset": offset, "ms": elapsed, "items": len(page["items"])})

report = {
    "dataset": {
        "projects": len(projects),
        "members": len(members),
        "tasks": len(checklist),
        "completed_tasks": len([i for i in range(200) if i % 5 == 0]),
        "alpha_tasks": 67,
    },
    "health": timed("GET", "/health", token=None),
    "projects_list": timed("GET", "/projects?limit=20", token),
    "members_list_first_page": timed("GET", "/members?limit=20", token),
    "members_list_last_page": timed("GET", "/members?limit=20&offset=40", token),
    "tasks_first_page": timed("GET", f"/tasks?project_id={alpha}&limit=20", token),
    "tasks_last_page": timed(
        "GET", f"/tasks?project_id={alpha}&limit=20&offset=60", token
    ),
    "dashboard": timed("GET", f"/analytics/dashboard?project_id={alpha}", token),
    "notifications": timed("GET", "/notifications?limit=20", token),
    "task_full_paging": {
        "pages": paging,
        "total_ms": round(sum(page["ms"] for page in paging), 2),
        "rows": sum(page["items"] for page in paging),
    },
}
print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))

"""SMTP notification tests: configuration, sending, and failure isolation."""
from email.message import EmailMessage

import pytest

from app.services import email_service


class FakeSMTP:
    """Minimal smtplib.SMTP double recording the session."""

    instances = []

    def __init__(self, host, port, timeout=10):
        self.host = host
        self.port = port
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.started_tls = False
        self.logged_in = None
        self.message = None
        self.closed = False
        FakeSMTP.instances.append(self)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc_info):
        self.closed = True
        return False

    def starttls(self):
        self.started_tls = True

    def login(self, user, password):
        self.logged_in = (user, password)

    def send_message(self, message: EmailMessage):
        self.message = message


class FailingSMTP(FakeSMTP):
    def send_message(self, message):
        raise OSError("SMTP is down")
